  [inst_3 :
    @MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure.{u_2} Ω₀₂ (@MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.toMeasurableSpace.{u_2} Ω₀₂ inst_1)
      (@MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume.{u_2} Ω₀₂ inst_1)]
  {G : Type uG} [inst_4 : AddCommGroup.{uG} G]
  [inst_5 :
    @Module.{0, uG} (ZMod (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat 2 (instOfNatNat 2))) G
      (@DivisionSemiring.toSemiring.{0} (ZMod (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat 2 (instOfNatNat 2)))
        (@Semifield.toDivisionSemiring.{0} (ZMod (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat 2 (instOfNatNat 2)))
          (@Field.toSemifield.{0} (ZMod (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat 2 (instOfNatNat 2)))
            (@ZMod.instField (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat 2 (instOfNatNat 2)) Nat.fact_prime_two))))
      (@AddCommGroup.toAddCommMonoid.{uG} G inst_4)]
  [inst_6 : Fintype.{uG} G] [inst_7 : MeasurableSpace.{uG} G] [inst_8 : @MeasurableSingletonClass.{uG} G inst_7]
  (p : @refPackage.{uG, u_1, u_2} Ω₀₁ Ω₀₂ inst inst_1 G inst_7),
  @Exists.{uG + 2} (Type uG) fun (Ω : Type uG) =>
    @Exists.{uG + 1} (MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.{uG} Ω) fun (x : MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.{uG} Ω) =>
      @Exists.{uG + 1} (Ω → G) fun (X₁ : Ω → G) =>
        @Exists.{uG + 1} (Ω → G) fun (X₂ : Ω → G) =>
          And (@Measurable.{uG, uG} Ω G (@MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.toMeasurableSpace.{uG} Ω x) inst_7 X₁)
            (And (@Measurable.{uG, uG} Ω G (@MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.toMeasurableSpace.{uG} Ω x) inst_7 X₂)
              (And
                (@MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure.{uG} Ω (@MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.toMeasurableSpace.{uG} Ω x)
                  (@MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume.{uG} Ω x))
                (And (@tau_minimizes.{uG, u_1, u_2, uG} Ω₀₁ Ω₀₂ inst inst_1 G inst_4 inst_7 p Ω x X₁ X₂)
                  (@Eq.{1} Real
                    (@rdist.{uG, uG, uG} Ω Ω G (@MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.toMeasurableSpace.{uG} Ω x)
                      (@MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.toMeasurableSpace.{uG} Ω x) inst_7 inst_4 X₁ X₂
                      (@MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume.{uG} Ω x) (@MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume.{uG} Ω x))

result.statement: For $\eta = 1/8$, there exist tau-minimizers $X_1, X_2$ satisfying $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
result.proof: For each $\eta <1/8$, consider minimizers $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ from \Cref{tau-min}. By \Cref{de-prop-improv}, they satisfy $d[X_1^\eta ; X_2^\eta ]=0$. By compactness of the space of probability measures on $G$, one may extract a converging subsequence of the distributions of $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ as $\eta \to 1/8$. By continuity of all the involved quantities, the limit is a pair of tau-minimizers for $1/8$ satisfying additionally $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.

declarations.name: tau
declarations.source_snippet:
noncomputable def tau {Ω₁ Ω₂ : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω₁] [MeasurableSpace Ω₂]
    (X₁ : Ω₁ → G) (X₂ : Ω₂ → G) (μ₁ : Measure Ω₁) (μ₂ : Measure Ω₂) : ℝ :=
  d[X₁ ; μ₁ # X₂ ; μ₂] + p.η * d[p.X₀₁ ; ℙ # X₁ ; μ₁] + p.η * d[p.X₀₂ ; ℙ # X₂ ; μ₂]

@[inherit_doc tau]
notation3:max "τ[" X₁ " ; " μ₁ " # " X₂ " ; " μ₂ " | " p"]" => tau p X₁ X₂ μ₁ μ₂

@[inherit_doc tau]
notation3:max "τ[" X₁ " # " X₂ " | " p"]" => tau p X₁ X₂ MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume
declarations.doc:
If $X_1,X_2$ are two $G$-valued random variables, then
$$ \tau[X_1; X_2] := d[X_1; X_2] + \eta d[X^0_1; X_1] + \eta d[X^0_2; X_2].$$
Here, $X^0_1$ and $X^0_2$ are two random variables fixed once and for all in most of the argument.
To lighten notation, We package `X^0_1` and `X^0_2` in a single object named `p`.

We denote it as `τ[X₁ ; μ₁ # X₂ ; μ₂ | p]` where `p` is a fixed package containing the information
of the reference random variables. When the measurable spaces have a canonical measure `ℙ`, we
can use `τ[X₁ # X₂ | p]`

declarations.source_snippet:
structure refPackage where
  /-- The first variable in a package. -/
  X₀₁ : Ω₀₁ → G
  /-- The second variable in a package. -/
  X₀₂ : Ω₀₂ → G
  hmeas1 : Measurable X₀₁
  hmeas2 : Measurable X₀₂
  /-- The constant that parameterizes how good the package is. The argument only works for
  small enough `η`, typically `≤ 1/9` or `< 1/8`. -/
  η : ℝ
  hη : 0 < η
  hη' : 8 * η ≤ 1

variable (p : refPackage Ω₀₁ Ω₀₂ G)
variable {Ω₀₁ Ω₀₂ G}

variable {Ω Ω' Ω₁ Ω₂ Ω'₁ Ω'₂ S T : Type*}

/-- If $X_1,X_2$ are two $G$-valued random variables, then
$$ \tau[X_1; X_2] := d[X_1; X_2] + \eta d[X^0_1; X_1] + \eta d[X^0_2; X_2].$$
Here, $X^0_1$ and $X^0_2$ are two random variables fixed once and for all in most of the argument.
To lighten notation, We package `X^0_1` and `X^0_2` in a single object named `p`.

We denote it as `τ[X₁ ; μ₁ # X₂ ; μ₂ | p]` where `p` is a fixed package containing the information
of the reference random variables. When the measurable spaces have a canonical measure `ℙ`, we
can use `τ[X₁ # X₂ | p]`
-/
declarations.doc:
A structure that packages all the fixed information in the main argument. In this way, when
defining the τ functional, we will only only need to refer to the package once in the notation
instead of stating the reference spaces, the reference measures and the reference random
variables.

The η parameter has now been incorporated into the package, in preparation for being able to
manipulate the package.

declarations.name: Mathlib.Tactic.RPowRing.Config
declarations.source_snippet:
structure Config where
  /-- the reducibility setting to use when comparing atoms for defeq -/
  red := TransparencyMode.reducible
  -- /-- if true, atoms inside ring expressions will be reduced recursively -/
  -- recursive := true
  deriving Inhabited, BEq, Repr

/-- Function elaborating `RingNF.Config`. -/
declare_config_elab elabConfig Config

/-- The monad for `RingNF` contains, in addition to the `AtomM` state,
a simp context for the main traversal and a simp function (which has another simp context)
to simplify normalized polynomials. -/
declarations.doc: Configuration for `ring_nf`.

declarations.name: Mathlib.Tactic.RPowRing.rpowRingTarget
declarations.source_snippet:
def rpowRingTarget (s : IO.Ref AtomM.State) (cfg : Config) : TacticM Unit := withMainContext do
  let goal ← getMainGoal
  let tgt ← instantiateMVars (← goal.getType)
  let r ← M.run s cfg <| rewrite tgt
  if r.expr.consumeMData.isConstOf ``True then
    goal.assign (← mkOfEqTrue (← r.getProof))
    replaceMainGoal []
  else
    replaceMainGoal [← applySimpResultToTarget goal tgt r]

/-- Use `rpow_ring` to rewrite hypothesis `h`. -/
declarations.doc: Use `rpow_ring` to rewrite the main goal.

declarations.name: Mathlib.Tactic.RPowRing.rpowRingLocalDecl
declarations.source_snippet:
def rpowRingLocalDecl (s : IO.Ref AtomM.State) (cfg : Config) (fvarId : FVarId) :
    TacticM Unit := withMainContext do
  let tgt ← instantiateMVars (← fvarId.getType)
  let goal ← getMainGoal
  let myres ← M.run s cfg <| rewrite tgt
  match ← applySimpResultToLocalDecl goal fvarId myres false with
  | none => replaceMainGoal []
  | some (_, newGoal) => replaceMainGoal [newGoal]

/--
Simplification tactic for expressions in the language of commutative (semi)rings,
which rewrites all ring expressions into a normal form.
* `rpow_ring!` will use a more aggressive reducibility setting to identify atoms.
* `rpow_ring (config := cfg)` allows for additional configuration:
  * `red`: the reducibility setting (overridden by `!`)
  * `recursive`: if true, `rpow_ring` will also recurse into atoms
* `rpow_ring` works as both a tactic and a conv tactic.
  In tactic mode, `rpow_ring at h` can be used to rewrite in a hypothesis.
-/
elab (name := rpowRing) "rpow_ring" tk:"!"? cfg:(config ?) loc:(location)? : tactic => do
  let mut cfg ← elabConfig cfg
  if tk.isSome then cfg := { cfg with red := .default }
  let loc := (loc.map expandLocation).getD (.targets #[] true)
  let s ← IO.mkRef {}
  withLocation loc (rpowRingLocalDecl s cfg) (rpowRingTarget s cfg)
    fun _ ↦ throwError "rpow_ring failed"

declarations.name: Simps.headStructureEtaReduce
declarations.source_snippet:
partial def headStructureEtaReduce (e : Expr) : MetaM Expr := do
  let env ← getEnv
  let (ctor, args) := e.getAppFnArgs
  let some (.ctorInfo { induct := struct, numParams, ..}) := env.find? ctor | pure e
  let some { fieldNames, .. } := getStructureInfo? env struct | pure e
  let (params, fields) := args.toList.splitAt numParams                                            
  trace[simps.debug]
    "rhs is constructor application with params{indentD params}\nand fields {indentD fields}"
  let field0 :: fieldsTail := fields | return e
  let fieldName0 :: fieldNamesTail := fieldNames.toList | return e
  let (fn0, fieldArgs0) := field0.getAppFnArgs
  unless fn0 == struct ++ fieldName0 do
    trace[simps.debug] "{fn0} ≠ {struct ++ fieldName0}"
    return e
  let (params', reduct :: _) := fieldArgs0.toList.splitAt numParams | unreachable!
  unless params' == params do
    trace[simps.debug] "{params'} ≠ {params}"
    return e
  trace[simps.debug] "Potential structure-eta-reduct:{indentExpr e}\nto{indentExpr reduct}"
  let allArgs := params.toArray.push reduct
  let isEta ← (fieldsTail.zip fieldNamesTail).allM fun (field, fieldName) ↦
    if field.getAppFnArgs == (struct ++ fieldName, allArgs) then pure true else isProof field
  unless isEta do return e
  trace[simps.debug] "Structure-eta-reduce:{indentExpr e}\nto{indentExpr reduct}"
  headStructureEtaReduce reduct
declarations.doc:
Perform head-structure-eta-reduction on expression `e`. That is, if `e` is of the form
`⟨f.1, f.2, ..., f.n⟩` with `f` definitionally equal to `e`, then
`headStructureEtaReduce e = headStructureEtaReduce f` and `headStructureEtaReduce e = e` otherwise.

declarations.name: Besicovitch.BallPackage
declarations.source_snippet:
structure BallPackage (β : Type*) (α : Type*) where
  c : β → α
  r : β → ℝ
  rpos : ∀ b, 0 < r b
  r_bound : ℝ
  r_le : ∀ b, r b ≤ r_bound
declarations.doc: A ball package is a family of balls in a metric space with positive bounded radii.

declarations.name: Besicovitch.TauPackage
declarations.source_snippet:
structure TauPackage (β : Type*) (α : Type*) extends BallPackage β α where
  τ : ℝ
  one_lt_tau : 1 < τ
declarations.doc:
A Besicovitch tau-package is a family of balls in a metric space with positive bounded radii,
together with enough data to proceed with the Besicovitch greedy algorithm. We register this in
a single structure to make sure that all our constructions in this algorithm only depend on
one variable.

declarations.name: Besicovitch.unitBallPackage
declarations.source_snippet:
def unitBallPackage (α : Type*) : BallPackage α α where
  c := id
  r _ := 1
  rpos _ := zero_lt_one
  r_bound := 1
  r_le _ := le_rfl
declarations.doc: The ball package made of unit balls.

declarations.name: exists_norm_eq_iInf_of_complete_convex
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem exists_norm_eq_iInf_of_complete_convex {K : Set F} (ne : K.Nonempty) (h₁ : IsComplete K)
    (h₂ : Convex ℝ K) : ∀ u : F, ∃ v ∈ K, ‖u - v‖ = ⨅ w : K, ‖u - w‖
declarations.doc:
Existence of minimizers
Let `u` be a point in a real inner product space, and let `K` be a nonempty complete convex subset.
Then there exists a (unique) `v` in `K` that minimizes the distance `‖u - v‖` to `u`.

declarations.name: exists_norm_eq_iInf_of_complete_subspace
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem exists_norm_eq_iInf_of_complete_subspace (h : IsComplete (↑K : Set E)) :
    ∀ u : E, ∃ v ∈ K, ‖u - v‖ = ⨅ w : (K : Set E), ‖u - w‖
declarations.doc:
Existence of projections on complete subspaces.
Let `u` be a point in an inner product space, and let `K` be a nonempty complete subspace.
Then there exists a (unique) `v` in `K` that minimizes the distance `‖u - v‖` to `u`.
This point `v` is usually called the orthogonal projection of `u` onto `K`.

declarations.name: norm_eq_iInf_iff_inner_eq_zero
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem norm_eq_iInf_iff_inner_eq_zero {u : E} {v : E} (hv : v ∈ K) :
    (‖u - v‖ = ⨅ w : K, ‖u - w‖) ↔ ∀ w ∈ K, ⟪u - v, w⟫ = 0
declarations.doc:
Characterization of minimizers in the projection on a subspace.
Let `u` be a point in an inner product space, and let `K` be a nonempty subspace.
Then point `v` minimizes the distance `‖u - v‖` over points in `K` if and only if
for all `w ∈ K`, `⟪u - v, w⟫ = 0` (i.e., `u - v` is orthogonal to the subspace `K`)

def tau_minimizes {Ω : Type*} [MeasureSpace Ω] (X₁ : Ω → G) (X₂ : Ω → G) : Prop :=
  ∀ (ν₁ : Measure G) (ν₂ : Measure G), IsProbabilityMeasure ν₁ → IsProbabilityMeasure ν₂ →
      τ[X₁ # X₂ | p] ≤ τ[id ; ν₁ # id ; ν₂ | p]

declarations.doc:
Property recording the fact that two random variables minimize the tau functional. Expressed
in terms of measures on the group to avoid quantifying over all spaces, but this implies comparison
with any pair of random variables, see Lemma `is_tau_min`.

declarations.name: isUniform_sub_const_of_rdist_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
If `d[X # X] = 0`, then `X - x₀` is the uniform distribution on the subgroup of `G`
stabilizing the distribution of `X`, for any `x₀` of positive probability.

declarations.name: norm_eq_iInf_iff_inner_eq_zero
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem norm_eq_iInf_iff_inner_eq_zero {u : E} {v : E} (hv : v ∈ K) :
    (‖u - v‖ = ⨅ w : K, ‖u - w‖) ↔ ∀ w ∈ K, ⟪u - v, w⟫ = 0
declarations.doc:
Characterization of minimizers in the projection on a subspace.
Let `u` be a point in an inner product space, and let `K` be a nonempty subspace.
Then point `v` minimizes the distance `‖u - v‖` over points in `K` if and only if
for all `w ∈ K`, `⟪u - v, w⟫ = 0` (i.e., `u - v` is orthogonal to the subspace `K`)

declarations.name: norm_eq_iInf_iff_real_inner_eq_zero
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem norm_eq_iInf_iff_real_inner_eq_zero (K : Submodule ℝ F) {u : F} {v : F} (hv : v ∈ K) :
    (‖u - v‖ = ⨅ w : (↑K : Set F), ‖u - w‖) ↔ ∀ w ∈ K, ⟪u - v, w⟫_ℝ = 0
declarations.doc:
Characterization of minimizers in the projection on a subspace, in the real case.
Let `u` be a point in a real inner product space, and let `K` be a nonempty subspace.
Then point `v` minimizes the distance `‖u - v‖` over points in `K` if and only if
for all `w ∈ K`, `⟪u - v, w⟫ = 0` (i.e., `u - v` is orthogonal to the subspace `K`).
This is superseded by `norm_eq_iInf_iff_inner_eq_zero` that gives the same conclusion over
any `RCLike` field.

declarations.name: Besicovitch.TauPackage
declarations.source_snippet:
structure TauPackage (β : Type*) (α : Type*) extends BallPackage β α where
  τ : ℝ
  one_lt_tau : 1 < τ
declarations.doc:
A Besicovitch tau-package is a family of balls in a metric space with positive bounded radii,
together with enough data to proceed with the Besicovitch greedy algorithm. We register this in
a single structure to make sure that all our constructions in this algorithm only depend on
one variable.

declarations.name: orthogonalProjection_minimal
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem orthogonalProjection_minimal {U : Submodule 𝕜 E} [HasOrthogonalProjection U] (y : E) :
    ‖y - orthogonalProjection U y‖ = ⨅ x : U, ‖y - x‖
declarations.doc: The orthogonal projection of `y` on `U` minimizes the distance `‖y - x‖` for `x ∈ U`.

result.statement: For $\eta = 1/8$, there exist tau-minimizers $X_1, X_2$ satisfying $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
result.proof: For each $\eta <1/8$, consider minimizers $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ from \Cref{tau-min}. By \Cref{de-prop-improv}, they satisfy $d[X_1^\eta ; X_2^\eta ]=0$. By compactness of the space of probability measures on $G$, one may extract a converging subsequence of the distributions of $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ as $\eta \to 1/8$. By continuity of all the involved quantities, the limit is a pair of tau-minimizers for $1/8$ satisfying additionally $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.

declarations.doc:
A Besicovitch tau-package is a family of balls in a metric space with positive bounded radii,
together with enough data to proceed with the Besicovitch greedy algorithm. We register this in
a single structure to make sure that all our constructions in this algorithm only depend on
one variable.

result.statement: For $\eta = 1/8$, there exist tau-minimizers $X_1, X_2$ satisfying $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
result.proof: For each $\eta <1/8$, consider minimizers $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ from \Cref{tau-min}. By \Cref{de-prop-improv}, they satisfy $d[X_1^\eta ; X_2^\eta ]=0$. By compactness of the space of probability measures on $G$, one may extract a converging subsequence of the distributions of $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ as $\eta \to 1/8$. By continuity of all the involved quantities, the limit is a pair of tau-minimizers for $1/8$ satisfying additionally $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.

variables.

The η parameter has now been incorporated into the package, in preparation for being able to
manipulate the package.

declarations.source_snippet:
def rpowRingTarget (s : IO.Ref AtomM.State) (cfg : Config) : TacticM Unit := withMainContext do
  let goal ← getMainGoal
  let tgt ← instantiateMVars (← goal.getType)
  let r ← M.run s cfg <| rewrite tgt
  if r.expr.consumeMData.isConstOf ``True then
    goal.assign (← mkOfEqTrue (← r.getProof))
    replaceMainGoal []
  else
    replaceMainGoal [← applySimpResultToTarget goal tgt r]

declarations.name: Mathlib.Tactic.RPowRing.rpowRingLocalDecl
declarations.source_snippet:
def rpowRingLocalDecl (s : IO.Ref AtomM.State) (cfg : Config) (fvarId : FVarId) :
    TacticM Unit := withMainContext do
  let tgt ← instantiateMVars (← fvarId.getType)
  let goal ← getMainGoal
  let myres ← M.run s cfg <| rewrite tgt
  match ← applySimpResultToLocalDecl goal fvarId myres false with
  | none => replaceMainGoal []
  | some (_, newGoal) => replaceMainGoal [newGoal]

/--
Simplification tactic for expressions in the language of commutative (semi)rings,
which rewrites all ring expressions into a normal form.
* `rpow_ring!` will use a more aggressive reducibility setting to identify atoms.
* `rpow_ring (config := cfg)` allows for additional configuration:
  * `red`: the reducibility setting (overridden by `!`)
  * `recursive`: if true, `rpow_ring` will also recurse into atoms
* `rpow_ring` works as both a tactic and a conv tactic.
  In tactic mode, `rpow_ring at h` can be used to rewrite in a hypothesis.
-/
elab (name := rpowRing) "rpow_ring" tk:"!"? cfg:(config ?) loc:(location)? : tactic => do
  let mut cfg ← elabConfig cfg
  if tk.isSome then cfg := { cfg with red := .default }
  let loc := (loc.map expandLocation).getD (.targets #[] true)
  let s ← IO.mkRef {}
  withLocation loc (rpowRingLocalDecl s cfg) (rpowRingTarget s cfg)
    fun _ ↦ throwError "rpow_ring failed"

@[inherit_doc rpowRing] macro "rpow_ring!" cfg:(config)? loc:(location)? : tactic =>
  `(tactic| rpow_ring ! $(cfg)? $(loc)?)

@[inherit_doc rpowRing] syntax (name := rpowRingConv) "rpow_ring" "!"? (config)? : conv

declarations.doc:
If $T_1, T_2, T_3$ are $G$-valued random variables with $T_1+T_2+T_3=0$ holds identically and
$$ \delta := \sum_{1 \leq i < j \leq 3} I[T_i;T_j]$$
Then there exist random variables $T'_1, T'_2$ such that
$$ d[T'_1;T'_2] + \eta (d[X_1^0;T'_1] - d[X_1^0;X_1]) + \eta(d[X_2^0;T'_2] - d[X_2^0;X_2]) $$
is at most
$$ \delta + \eta ( d[X^0_1;T_1]-d[X^0_1;X_1]) + \eta (d[X^0_2;T_2]-d[X^0_2;X_2]) $$
$$ + \tfrac12 \eta I[T_1: T_3] + \tfrac12 \eta I[T_2: T_3].$$

    apply tendsto_finset_sum _ (fun i _hi ↦ ?_)

declarations.name: probabilityMeasureEquivStdSimplex
declarations.source_snippet:
noncomputable def probabilityMeasureEquivStdSimplex [Fintype X] [MeasurableSingletonClass X] :
    ProbabilityMeasure X ≃ stdSimplex ℝ X where
  toFun := by
    intro μ
    refine ⟨fun i ↦ (μ {i}).toReal, by simp, ?_⟩
    simp only
    rw [← NNReal.coe_sum, ProbabilityMeasure.coeFn_def,
      ← ENNReal.toNNReal_sum (fun a _ha ↦ by finiteness)]
    simp
  invFun := by
    intro p
    refine ⟨∑ i, ENNReal.ofReal ((p : X → ℝ) i) • Measure.dirac i, ⟨?_⟩⟩
    simp only [Measure.coe_finset_sum, Measure.coe_smul, Finset.sum_apply, Pi.smul_apply,
      measure_univ, smul_eq_mul, mul_one]
    rw [← ENNReal.toReal_eq_toReal (by simp [ENNReal.sum_eq_top]) ENNReal.one_ne_top,
        ENNReal.toReal_sum (by simp)]
    simp_rw [ENNReal.toReal_ofReal (p.2.1 _), p.2.2, ENNReal.one_toReal]
  left_inv := by
    intro μ
    ext s _hs
    conv_rhs => rw [← Measure.sum_smul_dirac (μ := (μ : Measure X))]
    simp
  right_inv := by
    rintro ⟨p, p_pos, hp⟩
    ext i
    simp only [ProbabilityMeasure.mk_apply, Measure.coe_finset_sum, Measure.coe_smul,
      Finset.sum_apply, Pi.smul_apply, MeasurableSet.singleton, Measure.dirac_apply', smul_eq_mul]
    rw [Finset.sum_eq_single_of_mem i (Finset.mem_univ i)]
    · simp only [Measure.smul_apply, MeasurableSet.singleton, Measure.dirac_apply',
        Set.mem_singleton_iff, Set.indicator_of_mem, Pi.one_apply, smul_eq_mul, mul_one]
      exact ENNReal.toReal_ofReal (p_pos i)
    · intro b _ bi
      simp [bi]
declarations.doc:
The canonical bijection between the set of probability measures on a fintype and the set of
nonnegative functions on the points adding up to one.

declarations.name: probabilityMeasureEquivStdSimplex
declarations.source_snippet:
noncomputable def probabilityMeasureEquivStdSimplex [Fintype X] [MeasurableSingletonClass X] :
    ProbabilityMeasure X ≃ stdSimplex ℝ X where
  toFun := by
    intro μ
    refine ⟨fun i ↦ (μ {i}).toReal, by simp, ?_⟩
    simp only
    rw [← NNReal.coe_sum, ProbabilityMeasure.coeFn_def,
      ← ENNReal.toNNReal_sum (fun a _ha ↦ by finiteness)]
    simp
  invFun := by
    intro p
    refine ⟨∑ i, ENNReal.ofReal ((p : X → ℝ) i) • Measure.dirac i, ⟨?_⟩⟩
    simp only [Measure.coe_finset_sum, Measure.coe_smul, Finset.sum_apply, Pi.smul_apply,
      measure_univ, smul_eq_mul, mul_one]
    rw [← ENNReal.toReal_eq_toReal (by simp [ENNReal.sum_eq_top]) ENNReal.one_ne_top,
        ENNReal.toReal_sum (by simp)]
    simp_rw [ENNReal.toReal_ofReal (p.2.1 _), p.2.2, ENNReal.one_toReal]
  left_inv := by
    intro μ
    ext s _hs
    conv_rhs => rw [← Measure.sum_smul_dirac (μ := (μ : Measure X))]
    simp
  right_inv := by
    rintro ⟨p, p_pos, hp⟩
    ext i
    simp only [ProbabilityMeasure.mk_apply, Measure.coe_finset_sum, Measure.coe_smul,
      Finset.sum_apply, Pi.smul_apply, MeasurableSet.singleton, Measure.dirac_apply', smul_eq_mul]
    rw [Finset.sum_eq_single_of_mem i (Finset.mem_univ i)]
    · simp only [Measure.smul_apply, MeasurableSet.singleton, Measure.dirac_apply',
        Set.mem_singleton_iff, Set.indicator_of_mem, Pi.one_apply, smul_eq_mul, mul_one]
      exact ENNReal.toReal_ofReal (p_pos i)
    · intro b _ bi
      simp [bi]

noncomputable def tau {Ω₁ Ω₂ : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω₁] [MeasurableSpace Ω₂]
    (X₁ : Ω₁ → G) (X₂ : Ω₂ → G) (μ₁ : Measure Ω₁) (μ₂ : Measure Ω₂) : ℝ :=
  d[X₁ ; μ₁ # X₂ ; μ₂] + p.η * d[p.X₀₁ ; ℙ # X₁ ; μ₁] + p.η * d[p.X₀₂ ; ℙ # X₂ ; μ₂]

declarations.doc:
If $X_1,X_2$ are two $G$-valued random variables, then
$$ \tau[X_1; X_2] := d[X_1; X_2] + \eta d[X^0_1; X_1] + \eta d[X^0_2; X_2].$$
Here, $X^0_1$ and $X^0_2$ are two random variables fixed once and for all in most of the argument.
To lighten notation, We package `X^0_1` and `X^0_2` in a single object named `p`.

We denote it as `τ[X₁ ; μ₁ # X₂ ; μ₂ | p]` where `p` is a fixed package containing the information
of the reference random variables. When the measurable spaces have a canonical measure `ℙ`, we
can use `τ[X₁ # X₂ | p]`

result.statement: For $\eta = 1/8$, there exist tau-minimizers $X_1, X_2$ satisfying $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
result.proof: For each $\eta <1/8$, consider minimizers $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ from \Cref{tau-min}. By \Cref{de-prop-improv}, they satisfy $d[X_1^\eta ; X_2^\eta ]=0$. By compactness of the space of probability measures on $G$, one may extract a converging subsequence of the distributions of $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ as $\eta \to 1/8$. By continuity of all the involved quantities, the limit is a pair of tau-minimizers for $1/8$ satisfying additionally $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.

declarations.name: TopologicalSpace.MetrizableSpace
declarations.source_snippet:
class MetrizableSpace (X : Type*) [t : TopologicalSpace X] : Prop where
  exists_metric : ∃ m : MetricSpace X, m.toUniformSpace.toTopologicalSpace = t
declarations.doc:
A topological space is metrizable if there exists a metric space structure compatible with the
topology. To endow such a space with a compatible distance, use

noncomputable def probabilityMeasureHomeoStdSimplex : ProbabilityMeasure X ≃ₜ stdSimplex ℝ X where
  __ := probabilityMeasureEquivStdSimplex
  continuous_toFun := by
    apply continuous_iff_continuousAt.2 (fun μ ↦ ?_)
    rw [ContinuousAt, tendsto_subtype_rng, tendsto_pi_nhds]
    intro i
    simpa using ((continuous_pmf_apply i).continuousAt (x := μ)).tendsto
  continuous_invFun := by
    apply continuous_iff_continuousAt.2 (fun p ↦ ?_)
    rw [ContinuousAt, ProbabilityMeasure.tendsto_iff_forall_lintegral_tendsto]
    intro f
    simp only [Equiv.invFun_as_coe, probabilityMeasureEquivStdSimplex_symm_coe_apply,
      lintegral_finset_sum_measure, lintegral_smul_measure, lintegral_dirac]
    apply tendsto_finset_sum _ (fun i _hi ↦ ?_)
    apply ENNReal.Tendsto.mul_const (ENNReal.tendsto_ofReal _) (by simp)
    exact ((continuous_apply i).tendsto _).comp (continuous_subtype_val.tendsto _)

declarations.name: probabilityMeasureEquivStdSimplex
declarations.source_snippet:
noncomputable def probabilityMeasureEquivStdSimplex [Fintype X] [MeasurableSingletonClass X] :
    ProbabilityMeasure X ≃ stdSimplex ℝ X where
  toFun := by
    intro μ
    refine ⟨fun i ↦ (μ {i}).toReal, by simp, ?_⟩
    simp only
    rw [← NNReal.coe_sum, ProbabilityMeasure.coeFn_def,
      ← ENNReal.toNNReal_sum (fun a _ha ↦ by finiteness)]
    simp
  invFun := by
    intro p
    refine ⟨∑ i, ENNReal.ofReal ((p : X → ℝ) i) • Measure.dirac i, ⟨?_⟩⟩
    simp only [Measure.coe_finset_sum, Measure.coe_smul, Finset.sum_apply, Pi.smul_apply,
      measure_univ, smul_eq_mul, mul_one]
    rw [← ENNReal.toReal_eq_toReal (by simp [ENNReal.sum_eq_top]) ENNReal.one_ne_top,
        ENNReal.toReal_sum (by simp)]
    simp_rw [ENNReal.toReal_ofReal (p.2.1 _), p.2.2, ENNReal.one_toReal]
  left_inv := by
    intro μ
    ext s _hs
    conv_rhs => rw [← Measure.sum_smul_dirac (μ := (μ : Measure X))]
    simp
  right_inv := by
    rintro ⟨p, p_pos, hp⟩
    ext i
    simp only [ProbabilityMeasure.mk_apply, Measure.coe_finset_sum, Measure.coe_smul,
      Finset.sum_apply, Pi.smul_apply, MeasurableSet.singleton, Measure.dirac_apply', smul_eq_mul]
    rw [Finset.sum_eq_single_of_mem i (Finset.mem_univ i)]
    · simp only [Measure.smul_apply, MeasurableSet.singleton, Measure.dirac_apply',
        Set.mem_singleton_iff, Set.indicator_of_mem, Pi.one_apply, smul_eq_mul, mul_one]
      exact ENNReal.toReal_ofReal (p_pos i)
    · intro b _ bi
      simp [bi]
declarations.doc:
The canonical bijection between the set of probability measures on a fintype and the set of
nonnegative functions on the points adding up to one.

    (fun p =>

        (∑ i : X, HSMul.hSMul.{0, u_1, u_1} (ENNReal.ofReal (↑p i)) (MeasureTheory.Measure.dirac.{u_1} i)) ⋯)

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure.continuous_map
declarations.source_snippet:
lemma continuous_map {f : Ω → Ω'} (f_cont : Continuous f) :
    Continuous (fun ν ↦ ProbabilityMeasure.map ν f_cont.measurable.aemeasurable)
declarations.doc:
If `f : X → Y` is continuous and `Y` is equipped with the Borel sigma algebra, then
the push-forward of probability measures `f* : ProbabilityMeasure X → ProbabilityMeasure Y`
is continuous (in the topologies of convergence in distribution).

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure.tendsto_map_of_tendsto_of_continuous
declarations.source_snippet:
lemma tendsto_map_of_tendsto_of_continuous {ι : Type*} {L : Filter ι}
    (νs : ι → ProbabilityMeasure Ω) (ν : ProbabilityMeasure Ω) (lim : Tendsto νs L (𝓝 ν))
    {f : Ω → Ω'} (f_cont : Continuous f) :
    Tendsto (fun i ↦ (νs i).map f_cont.measurable.aemeasurable) L
      (𝓝 (ν.map f_cont.measurable.aemeasurable))
declarations.doc:
If `f : X → Y` is continuous and `Y` is equipped with the Borel sigma algebra, then
convergence (in distribution) of `ProbabilityMeasure`s on `X` implies convergence (in
distribution) of the push-forwards of these measures by `f`.

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure.tendsto_iff_forall_lintegral_tendsto
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem tendsto_iff_forall_lintegral_tendsto {γ : Type*} {F : Filter γ}
    {μs : γ → ProbabilityMeasure Ω} {μ : ProbabilityMeasure Ω} :
    Tendsto μs F (𝓝 μ) ↔
      ∀ f : Ω →ᵇ ℝ≥0,
        Tendsto (fun i ↦ ∫⁻ ω, f ω ∂(μs i : Measure Ω)) F (𝓝 (∫⁻ ω, f ω ∂(μ : Measure Ω)))
declarations.doc:
A characterization of weak convergence of probability measures by the condition that the
integrals of every continuous bounded nonnegative function converge to the integral of the function
against the limit measure.

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure.t2Space
declarations.source_snippet: instance t2Space : T2Space (ProbabilityMeasure Ω)
declarations.doc:
On topological spaces where indicators of closed sets have decreasing approximating sequences of
continuous functions (`HasOuterApproxClosed`), the topology of convergence in distribution of Borel
probability measures is Hausdorff (`T2Space`).

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.levyProkhorovDist_pseudoMetricSpace_probabilityMeasure
declarations.source_snippet:
noncomputable instance levyProkhorovDist_pseudoMetricSpace_probabilityMeasure :
    PseudoMetricSpace (LevyProkhorov (ProbabilityMeasure Ω)) where
  dist μ ν
declarations.doc:
The Lévy-Prokhorov distance `levyProkhorovDist` makes `ProbabilityMeasure Ω` a pseudometric
space. The instance is recorded on the type synonym
`LevyProkhorov (ProbabilityMeasure Ω) := ProbabilityMeasure Ω`.

Note: For this pseudometric to give the topology of convergence in distribution, one must
furthermore assume that `Ω` is separable.

result.statement: For $\eta = 1/8$, there exist tau-minimizers $X_1, X_2$ satisfying $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
result.proof: For each $\eta <1/8$, consider minimizers $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ from \Cref{tau-min}. By \Cref{de-prop-improv}, they satisfy $d[X_1^\eta ; X_2^\eta ]=0$. By compactness of the space of probability measures on $G$, one may extract a converging subsequence of the distributions of $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ as $\eta \to 1/8$. By continuity of all the involved quantities, the limit is a pair of tau-minimizers for $1/8$ satisfying additionally $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.

declarations.name: IsSeqCompact
declarations.doc:
A set `s` is sequentially compact if every sequence taking values in `s` has a
converging subsequence.
declarations.type: {X : Type u_1} → [inst : TopologicalSpace.{u_1} X] → Set.{u_1} X → Prop

definition.value:
fun {X} [TopologicalSpace.{u_1} X] s =>
  ∀ ⦃x : Nat → X⦄,
    (∀ (n : Nat), Membership.mem.{u_1, u_1} s (x n)) →
      ∃ a,
        And (Membership.mem.{u_1, u_1} s a)
          (∃ φ,
            And (StrictMono.{0, 0} φ)
              (Filter.Tendsto.{0, u_1} (Function.comp.{1, 1, u_1 + 1} x φ) Filter.atTop.{0} (nhds.{u_1} a)))
definition.type: {X : Type u_1} → [inst : TopologicalSpace.{u_1} X] → Set.{u_1} X → Prop
definition.name: IsSeqCompact

declarations.conclusion: Prop

declarations.name: PFR_conjecture
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem PFR_conjecture (h₀A : A.Nonempty) (hA : Nat.card (A + A) ≤ K * Nat.card A) :
     ∃ (H : Submodule (ZMod 2) G) (c : Set G),
      Nat.card c < 2 * K ^ 12 ∧ Nat.card H ≤ Nat.card A ∧ A ⊆ c + H
declarations.doc:
The polynomial Freiman-Ruzsa (PFR) conjecture: if `A` is a subset of an elementary abelian
2-group of doubling constant at most `K`, then `A` can be covered by at most `2 * K ^ 12` cosets of
a subgroup of cardinality at most `|A|`.
declarations.type:
∀ {G : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup.{u_1} G] {A : Set.{u_1} G} {K : Real} [inst_1 : Countable.{u_1 + 1} G]
  [inst_2 : Module.{0, u_1} (ZMod 2) G] [inst_3 : Fintype.{u_1} G],
  Set.Nonempty.{u_1} A →
    LE.le.{0} (↑(Nat.card.{u_1} ↑(HAdd.hAdd.{u_1, u_1, u_1} A A))) (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} K ↑(Nat.card.{u_1} ↑A)) →
      ∃ H c,
        And (LT.lt.{0} (↑(Nat.card.{u_1} ↑c)) (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} 2 (HPow.hPow.{0, 0, 0} K 12)))
          (And (LE.le.{0} (Nat.card.{u_1} ↥H) (Nat.card.{u_1} ↑A))
            (HasSubset.Subset.{u_1} A (HAdd.hAdd.{u_1, u_1, u_1} c ↑H)))
declarations.conclusion:
∃ H c,
  And (LT.lt.{0} (↑(Nat.card.{u_1} ↑c)) (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} 2 (HPow.hPow.{0, 0, 0} K 12)))
    (And (LE.le.{0} (Nat.card.{u_1} ↥H) (Nat.card.{u_1} ↑A))
      (HasSubset.Subset.{u_1} A (HAdd.hAdd.{u_1, u_1, u_1} c ↑H)))

declarations.name: PFR_conjecture_aux
declarations.source_snippet:
lemma PFR_conjecture_aux (h₀A : A.Nonempty) (hA : Nat.card (A + A) ≤ K * Nat.card A) :
    ∃ (H : Submodule (ZMod 2) G) (c : Set G),
    Nat.card c ≤ K ^ (13/2 : ℝ) * Nat.card A ^ (1/2 : ℝ) * Nat.card H ^ (-1/2 : ℝ)
      ∧ Nat.card H ≤ K ^ 11 * Nat.card A ∧ Nat.card A ≤ K ^ 11 * Nat.card H ∧ A ⊆ c + H
declarations.doc:
Auxiliary statement towards the polynomial Freiman-Ruzsa (PFR) conjecture: if `A` is a subset of
an elementary abelian 2-group of doubling constant at most $K$, then there exists a subgroup `H`
such that `A` can be covered by at most `K^(13/2) |A|^(1/2) / |H|^(1/2)` cosets of `H`, and `H` has
the same cardinality as `A` up to a multiplicative factor `K^11`.
declarations.type:
∀ {G : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup.{u_1} G] {A : Set.{u_1} G} {K : Real} [inst_1 : Countable.{u_1 + 1} G]
  [inst_2 : Module.{0, u_1} (ZMod 2) G] [inst_3 : Fintype.{u_1} G],
  Set.Nonempty.{u_1} A →
    LE.le.{0} (↑(Nat.card.{u_1} ↑(HAdd.hAdd.{u_1, u_1, u_1} A A))) (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} K ↑(Nat.card.{u_1} ↑A)) →
      ∃ H c,
        And
          (LE.le.{0} (↑(Nat.card.{u_1} ↑c))
            (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0}
              (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} (HPow.hPow.{0, 0, 0} K (13 / 2))
                (HPow.hPow.{0, 0, 0} (↑(Nat.card.{u_1} ↑A)) (1 / 2)))
              (HPow.hPow.{0, 0, 0} (↑(Nat.card.{u_1} ↥H)) (-1 / 2))))
          (And (LE.le.{0} (↑(Nat.card.{u_1} ↥H)) (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} (HPow.hPow.{0, 0, 0} K 11) ↑(Nat.card.{u_1} ↑A)))
            (And
              (LE.le.{0} (↑(Nat.card.{u_1} ↑A)) (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} (HPow.hPow.{0, 0, 0} K 11) ↑(Nat.card.{u_1} ↥H)))
              (HasSubset.Subset.{u_1} A (HAdd.hAdd.{u_1, u_1, u_1} c ↑H))))
declarations.conclusion:
∃ H c,
  And
    (LE.le.{0} (↑(Nat.card.{u_1} ↑c))
      (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0}
        (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} (HPow.hPow.{0, 0, 0} K (13 / 2)) (HPow.hPow.{0, 0, 0} (↑(Nat.card.{u_1} ↑A)) (1 / 2)))
        (HPow.hPow.{0, 0, 0} (↑(Nat.card.{u_1} ↥H)) (-1 / 2))))
    (And (LE.le.{0} (↑(Nat.card.{u_1} ↥H)) (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} (HPow.hPow.{0, 0, 0} K 11) ↑(Nat.card.{u_1} ↑A)))
      (And (LE.le.{0} (↑(Nat.card.{u_1} ↑A)) (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} (HPow.hPow.{0, 0, 0} K 11) ↑(Nat.card.{u_1} ↥H)))
        (HasSubset.Subset.{u_1} A (HAdd.hAdd.{u_1, u_1, u_1} c ↑H))))

declarations.name: tendsto_div_of_monotone_of_exists_subseq_tendsto_div
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem tendsto_div_of_monotone_of_exists_subseq_tendsto_div (u : ℕ → ℝ) (l : ℝ)
    (hmono : Monotone u)
    (hlim : ∀ a : ℝ, 1 < a → ∃ c : ℕ → ℕ, (∀ᶠ n in atTop, (c (n + 1) : ℝ) ≤ a * c n) ∧
      Tendsto c atTop atTop ∧ Tendsto (fun n => u (c n) / c n) atTop (𝓝 l)) :
    Tendsto (fun n => u n / n) atTop (𝓝 l)
declarations.doc:
If a monotone sequence `u` is such that `u n / n` tends to a limit `l` along subsequences with
exponential growth rate arbitrarily close to `1`, then `u n / n` tends to `l`.

declarations.name: Filter.tendsto_atTop_of_monotone_of_filter
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem tendsto_atTop_of_monotone_of_filter [Preorder ι] [Preorder α] {l : Filter ι} {u : ι → α}
    (h : Monotone u) [NeBot l] (hu : Tendsto u l atTop) : Tendsto u atTop atTop
declarations.doc:
If a monotone function `u : ι → α` tends to `atTop` along *some* non-trivial filter `l`, then
it tends to `atTop` along `atTop`.

declarations.name: tendsto_div_of_monotone_of_tendsto_div_floor_pow
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem tendsto_div_of_monotone_of_tendsto_div_floor_pow (u : ℕ → ℝ) (l : ℝ) (hmono : Monotone u)
    (c : ℕ → ℝ) (cone : ∀ k, 1 < c k) (clim : Tendsto c atTop (𝓝 1))
    (hc : ∀ k, Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => u ⌊c k ^ n⌋₊ / ⌊c k ^ n⌋₊) atTop (𝓝 l)) :
    Tendsto (fun n => u n / n) atTop (𝓝 l)
declarations.doc:
If a monotone sequence `u` is such that `u ⌊c^n⌋₊ / ⌊c^n⌋₊` converges to a limit `l` for all
`c > 1`, then `u n / n` tends to `l`. It is even enough to have the assumption for a sequence of
`c`s converging to `1`.

declarations.name: Filter.tendsto_atTop_finset_of_monotone
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem tendsto_atTop_finset_of_monotone [Preorder β] {f : β → Finset α} (h : Monotone f)
    (h' : ∀ x : α, ∃ n, x ∈ f n) : Tendsto f atTop atTop
declarations.doc:
If `f` is a monotone sequence of `Finset`s and each `x` belongs to one of `f n`, then
`Tendsto f atTop atTop`.

declarations.name: Monotone.iUnion_comp_tendsto_atTop
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem _root_.Monotone.iUnion_comp_tendsto_atTop [Preorder β] {l : Filter α} [l.NeBot]
    {s : β → Set γ} (hs : Monotone s) {f : α → β} (hf : Tendsto f l atTop) :
    ⋃ a, s (f a) = ⋃ b, s b
declarations.doc:
If `s` is a monotone family of sets and `f` tends to `atTop` along a nontrivial filter,
then the indexed union of `s ∘ f` is equal to the indexed union of `s`.

result.statement: For $\eta = 1/8$, there exist tau-minimizers $X_1, X_2$ satisfying $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
result.proof: For each $\eta <1/8$, consider minimizers $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ from \Cref{tau-min}. By \Cref{de-prop-improv}, they satisfy $d[X_1^\eta ; X_2^\eta ]=0$. By compactness of the space of probability measures on $G$, one may extract a converging subsequence of the distributions of $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ as $\eta \to 1/8$. By continuity of all the involved quantities, the limit is a pair of tau-minimizers for $1/8$ satisfying additionally $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.

nodes.claim: For a sequence of pairs of probability measures on a finite discrete G, there is a converging subsequence in the weak topology of ProbabilityMeasure G × ProbabilityMeasure G.
nodes.body:
skip
classical
let h := probabilityMeasureHomeoStdSimplex (X := G)
have hc_simplex : CompactSpace (stdSimplex ℝ G) := by
  rw [← isCompact_univ_iff]
  rw [Subtype.isCompact_iff]
  simpa using isCompact_stdSimplex G
have hc : IsCompact (Set.univ : Set (stdSimplex ℝ G)) := isCompact_univ_iff.mpr hc_simplex
have hseq : IsSeqCompact (Set.univ : Set (stdSimplex ℝ G)) := UniformSpace.isCompact_iff_isSeqCompact.mp hc
rcases hseq (x := fun n => h (x n).1) (by intro n; trivial) with ⟨y₁, hy₁_mem, φ₁, hφ₁mono, hy₁⟩
let μ₁ : MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure G := h.symm y₁
have ht1 : Filter.Tendsto (fun n => (x (φ₁ n)).1) Filter.atTop (nhds μ₁) := by
  simpa [μ₁, Function.comp_def] using (h.symm.continuous.tendsto y₁).comp hy₁
rcases hseq (x := fun n => h (x (φ₁ n)).2) (by intro n; trivial) with ⟨y₂, hy₂_mem, φ₂, hφ₂mono, hy₂⟩
let μ₂ : MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure G := h.symm y₂
have ht2 : Filter.Tendsto (fun n => (x (φ₁ (φ₂ n))).2) Filter.atTop (nhds μ₂) := by
  simpa [μ₂, Function.comp_def] using (h.symm.continuous.tendsto y₂).comp hy₂
let φ : ℕ → ℕ := φ₁ ∘ φ₂
have hφmono : StrictMono φ := hφ₁mono.comp hφ₂mono
have ht1' : Filter.Tendsto (fun n => (x (φ n)).1) Filter.atTop (nhds μ₁) := by
  have ht := ht1.comp (StrictMono.tendsto_atTop hφ₂mono)
  simpa [φ, Function.comp_def] using ht
have ht2' : Filter.Tendsto (fun n => (x (φ n)).2) Filter.atTop (nhds μ₂) := by
  simpa [φ, Function.comp_def] using ht2
exact ⟨μ₁, μ₂, φ, hφmono, ht1', ht2'⟩

∀ {Ω₀₁ : Type u_1} {Ω₀₂ : Type u_2} [inst : MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.{u_1} Ω₀₁]
  [inst_1 : MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.{u_2} Ω₀₂]
  [inst_2 :

      (@MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume.{u_1} Ω₀₁ inst)]
  [inst_3 :
    @MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure.{u_2} Ω₀₂ (@MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.toMeasurableSpace.{u_2} Ω₀₂ inst_1)
      (@MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume.{u_2} Ω₀₂ inst_1)]
  {G : Type uG} [inst_4 : AddCommGroup.{uG} G]
  [inst_5 :
    @Module.{0, uG} (ZMod (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat 2 (instOfNatNat 2))) G
      (@DivisionSemiring.toSemiring.{0} (ZMod (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat 2 (instOfNatNat 2)))
        (@Semifield.toDivisionSemiring.{0} (ZMod (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat 2 (instOfNatNat 2)))
          (@Field.toSemifield.{0} (ZMod (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat 2 (instOfNatNat 2)))
            (@ZMod.instField (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat 2 (instOfNatNat 2)) Nat.fact_prime_two))))
      (@AddCommGroup.toAddCommMonoid.{uG} G inst_4)]
  [inst_6 : Fintype.{uG} G] [inst_7 : MeasurableSpace.{uG} G] [inst_8 : @MeasurableSingletonClass.{uG} G inst_7]
  (p : @refPackage.{uG, u_1, u_2} Ω₀₁ Ω₀₂ inst inst_1 G inst_7),
  @Exists.{uG + 2} (Type uG) fun (Ω : Type uG) =>
    @Exists.{uG + 1} (MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.{uG} Ω) fun (x : MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.{uG} Ω) =>
      @Exists.{uG + 1} (Ω → G) fun (X₁ : Ω → G) =>
        @Exists.{uG + 1} (Ω → G) fun (X₂ : Ω → G) =>
          And (@Measurable.{uG, uG} Ω G (@MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.toMeasurableSpace.{uG} Ω x) inst_7 X₁)
            (And (@Measurable.{uG, uG} Ω G (@MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.toMeasurableSpace.{uG} Ω x) inst_7 X₂)
              (And
                (@MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure.{uG} Ω (@MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.toMeasurableSpace.{uG} Ω x)
                  (@MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume.{uG} Ω x))
                (And (@tau_minimizes.{uG, u_1, u_2, uG} Ω₀₁ Ω₀₂ inst inst_1 G inst_4 inst_7 p Ω x X₁ X₂)
                  (@Eq.{1} Real
                    (@rdist.{uG, uG, uG} Ω Ω G (@MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.toMeasurableSpace.{uG} Ω x)
                      (@MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.toMeasurableSpace.{uG} Ω x) inst_7 inst_4 X₁ X₂
                      (@MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume.{uG} Ω x) (@MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume.{uG} Ω x))
                    (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Real 0 (@Zero.toOfNat0.{0} Real Real.instZero))))))

    {G : Type uG} [AddCommGroup G] [Module (ZMod 2) G] [Fintype G] [MeasurableSpace G]
    [MeasurableSingletonClass G] (q : refPackage Ω₀₁ Ω₀₂ G) (hq : 8 * q.η < 1) :

    {G : Type uG} [Fintype G] [MeasurableSpace G] [MeasurableSingletonClass G]

nodes.claim: For a sequence of pairs of probability measures on a finite discrete G, there is a converging subsequence in the weak topology of ProbabilityMeasure G × ProbabilityMeasure G.
nodes.body:
skip
classical
let h := probabilityMeasureHomeoStdSimplex (X := G)
have hc_simplex : CompactSpace (stdSimplex ℝ G) := by
  rw [← isCompact_univ_iff]
  rw [Subtype.isCompact_iff]
  simpa using isCompact_stdSimplex G
have hc : IsCompact (Set.univ : Set (stdSimplex ℝ G)) := isCompact_univ_iff.mpr hc_simplex
have hseq : IsSeqCompact (Set.univ : Set (stdSimplex ℝ G)) := UniformSpace.isCompact_iff_isSeqCompact.mp hc
rcases hseq (x := fun n => h (x n).1) (by intro n; trivial) with ⟨y₁, hy₁_mem, φ₁, hφ₁mono, hy₁⟩
let μ₁ : MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure G := h.symm y₁
have ht1 : Filter.Tendsto (fun n => (x (φ₁ n)).1) Filter.atTop (nhds μ₁) := by
  simpa [μ₁, Function.comp_def] using (h.symm.continuous.tendsto y₁).comp hy₁
rcases hseq (x := fun n => h (x (φ₁ n)).2) (by intro n; trivial) with ⟨y₂, hy₂_mem, φ₂, hφ₂mono, hy₂⟩
let μ₂ : MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure G := h.symm y₂
have ht2 : Filter.Tendsto (fun n => (x (φ₁ (φ₂ n))).2) Filter.atTop (nhds μ₂) := by
  simpa [μ₂, Function.comp_def] using (h.symm.continuous.tendsto y₂).comp hy₂
let φ : ℕ → ℕ := φ₁ ∘ φ₂
have hφmono : StrictMono φ := hφ₁mono.comp hφ₂mono
have ht1' : Filter.Tendsto (fun n => (x (φ n)).1) Filter.atTop (nhds μ₁) := by
  have ht := ht1.comp (StrictMono.tendsto_atTop hφ₂mono)
  simpa [φ, Function.comp_def] using ht
have ht2' : Filter.Tendsto (fun n => (x (φ n)).2) Filter.atTop (nhds μ₂) := by
  simpa [φ, Function.comp_def] using ht2
exact ⟨μ₁, μ₂, φ, hφmono, ht1', ht2'⟩

$$ \tau[X_1; X_2] := d[X_1; X_2] + \eta d[X^0_1; X_1] + \eta d[X^0_2; X_2].$$
Here, $X^0_1$ and $X^0_2$ are two random variables fixed once and for all in most of the argument.

We denote it as `τ[X₁ ; μ₁ # X₂ ; μ₂ | p]` where `p` is a fixed package containing the information
of the reference random variables. When the measurable spaces have a canonical measure `ℙ`, we
can use `τ[X₁ # X₂ | p]`
-/
declarations.doc:
A structure that packages all the fixed information in the main argument. In this way, when
defining the τ functional, we will only only need to refer to the package once in the notation
instead of stating the reference spaces, the reference measures and the reference random
variables.

The η parameter has now been incorporated into the package, in preparation for being able to
manipulate the package.

declarations.source_snippet:
def rpowRingTarget (s : IO.Ref AtomM.State) (cfg : Config) : TacticM Unit := withMainContext do
  let goal ← getMainGoal
  let tgt ← instantiateMVars (← goal.getType)
  let r ← M.run s cfg <| rewrite tgt
  if r.expr.consumeMData.isConstOf ``True then
    goal.assign (← mkOfEqTrue (← r.getProof))
    replaceMainGoal []
  else
    replaceMainGoal [← applySimpResultToTarget goal tgt r]

declarations.name: Mathlib.Tactic.RPowRing.rpowRingLocalDecl
declarations.source_snippet:
def rpowRingLocalDecl (s : IO.Ref AtomM.State) (cfg : Config) (fvarId : FVarId) :
    TacticM Unit := withMainContext do
  let tgt ← instantiateMVars (← fvarId.getType)
  let goal ← getMainGoal
  let myres ← M.run s cfg <| rewrite tgt
  match ← applySimpResultToLocalDecl goal fvarId myres false with
  | none => replaceMainGoal []
  | some (_, newGoal) => replaceMainGoal [newGoal]

/--
Simplification tactic for expressions in the language of commutative (semi)rings,
which rewrites all ring expressions into a normal form.
* `rpow_ring!` will use a more aggressive reducibility setting to identify atoms.
* `rpow_ring (config := cfg)` allows for additional configuration:
  * `red`: the reducibility setting (overridden by `!`)
  * `recursive`: if true, `rpow_ring` will also recurse into atoms
* `rpow_ring` works as both a tactic and a conv tactic.
  In tactic mode, `rpow_ring at h` can be used to rewrite in a hypothesis.
-/
elab (name := rpowRing) "rpow_ring" tk:"!"? cfg:(config ?) loc:(location)? : tactic => do
  let mut cfg ← elabConfig cfg
  if tk.isSome then cfg := { cfg with red := .default }
  let loc := (loc.map expandLocation).getD (.targets #[] true)
  let s ← IO.mkRef {}
  withLocation loc (rpowRingLocalDecl s cfg) (rpowRingTarget s cfg)
    fun _ ↦ throwError "rpow_ring failed"

@[inherit_doc rpowRing] macro "rpow_ring!" cfg:(config)? loc:(location)? : tactic =>
  `(tactic| rpow_ring ! $(cfg)? $(loc)?)

@[inherit_doc rpowRing] syntax (name := rpowRingConv) "rpow_ring" "!"? (config)? : conv

declarations.doc:
If $T_1, T_2, T_3$ are $G$-valued random variables with $T_1+T_2+T_3=0$ holds identically and
$$ \delta := \sum_{1 \leq i < j \leq 3} I[T_i;T_j]$$
Then there exist random variables $T'_1, T'_2$ such that
$$ d[T'_1;T'_2] + \eta (d[X_1^0;T'_1] - d[X_1^0;X_1]) + \eta(d[X_2^0;T'_2] - d[X_2^0;X_2]) $$
is at most
$$ \delta + \eta ( d[X^0_1;T_1]-d[X^0_1;X_1]) + \eta (d[X^0_2;T_2]-d[X^0_2;X_2]) $$
$$ + \tfrac12 \eta I[T_1: T_3] + \tfrac12 \eta I[T_2: T_3].$$

result.statement: For $\eta = 1/8$, there exist tau-minimizers $X_1, X_2$ satisfying $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
result.proof: For each $\eta <1/8$, consider minimizers $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ from \Cref{tau-min}. By \Cref{de-prop-improv}, they satisfy $d[X_1^\eta ; X_2^\eta ]=0$. By compactness of the space of probability measures on $G$, one may extract a converging subsequence of the distributions of $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ as $\eta \to 1/8$. By continuity of all the involved quantities, the limit is a pair of tau-minimizers for $1/8$ satisfying additionally $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.

declarations.name: PFR_conjecture
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem PFR_conjecture (h₀A : A.Nonempty) (hA : Nat.card (A + A) ≤ K * Nat.card A) :
     ∃ (H : Submodule (ZMod 2) G) (c : Set G),
      Nat.card c < 2 * K ^ 12 ∧ Nat.card H ≤ Nat.card A ∧ A ⊆ c + H
declarations.doc:
The polynomial Freiman-Ruzsa (PFR) conjecture: if `A` is a subset of an elementary abelian
2-group of doubling constant at most `K`, then `A` can be covered by at most `2 * K ^ 12` cosets of
a subgroup of cardinality at most `|A|`.
declarations.type:
∀ {G : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup.{u_1} G] {A : Set.{u_1} G} {K : Real} [inst_1 : Countable.{u_1 + 1} G]
  [inst_2 : Module.{0, u_1} (ZMod 2) G] [inst_3 : Fintype.{u_1} G],
  Set.Nonempty.{u_1} A →
    LE.le.{0} (↑(Nat.card.{u_1} ↑(HAdd.hAdd.{u_1, u_1, u_1} A A))) (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} K ↑(Nat.card.{u_1} ↑A)) →
      ∃ H c,
        And (LT.lt.{0} (↑(Nat.card.{u_1} ↑c)) (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} 2 (HPow.hPow.{0, 0, 0} K 12)))
          (And (LE.le.{0} (Nat.card.{u_1} ↥H) (Nat.card.{u_1} ↑A))
            (HasSubset.Subset.{u_1} A (HAdd.hAdd.{u_1, u_1, u_1} c ↑H)))
declarations.conclusion:
∃ H c,
  And (LT.lt.{0} (↑(Nat.card.{u_1} ↑c)) (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} 2 (HPow.hPow.{0, 0, 0} K 12)))
    (And (LE.le.{0} (Nat.card.{u_1} ↥H) (Nat.card.{u_1} ↑A))
      (HasSubset.Subset.{u_1} A (HAdd.hAdd.{u_1, u_1, u_1} c ↑H)))

declarations.name: PFR_conjecture_aux
declarations.source_snippet:
lemma PFR_conjecture_aux (h₀A : A.Nonempty) (hA : Nat.card (A + A) ≤ K * Nat.card A) :
    ∃ (H : Submodule (ZMod 2) G) (c : Set G),
    Nat.card c ≤ K ^ (13/2 : ℝ) * Nat.card A ^ (1/2 : ℝ) * Nat.card H ^ (-1/2 : ℝ)
      ∧ Nat.card H ≤ K ^ 11 * Nat.card A ∧ Nat.card A ≤ K ^ 11 * Nat.card H ∧ A ⊆ c + H
declarations.doc:
Auxiliary statement towards the polynomial Freiman-Ruzsa (PFR) conjecture: if `A` is a subset of
an elementary abelian 2-group of doubling constant at most $K$, then there exists a subgroup `H`
such that `A` can be covered by at most `K^(13/2) |A|^(1/2) / |H|^(1/2)` cosets of `H`, and `H` has
the same cardinality as `A` up to a multiplicative factor `K^11`.
declarations.type:
∀ {G : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup.{u_1} G] {A : Set.{u_1} G} {K : Real} [inst_1 : Countable.{u_1 + 1} G]
  [inst_2 : Module.{0, u_1} (ZMod 2) G] [inst_3 : Fintype.{u_1} G],
  Set.Nonempty.{u_1} A →
    LE.le.{0} (↑(Nat.card.{u_1} ↑(HAdd.hAdd.{u_1, u_1, u_1} A A))) (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} K ↑(Nat.card.{u_1} ↑A)) →
      ∃ H c,
        And
          (LE.le.{0} (↑(Nat.card.{u_1} ↑c))
            (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0}
              (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} (HPow.hPow.{0, 0, 0} K (13 / 2))
                (HPow.hPow.{0, 0, 0} (↑(Nat.card.{u_1} ↑A)) (1 / 2)))
              (HPow.hPow.{0, 0, 0} (↑(Nat.card.{u_1} ↥H)) (-1 / 2))))
          (And (LE.le.{0} (↑(Nat.card.{u_1} ↥H)) (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} (HPow.hPow.{0, 0, 0} K 11) ↑(Nat.card.{u_1} ↑A)))
            (And
              (LE.le.{0} (↑(Nat.card.{u_1} ↑A)) (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} (HPow.hPow.{0, 0, 0} K 11) ↑(Nat.card.{u_1} ↥H)))
              (HasSubset.Subset.{u_1} A (HAdd.hAdd.{u_1, u_1, u_1} c ↑H))))
declarations.conclusion:
∃ H c,
  And
    (LE.le.{0} (↑(Nat.card.{u_1} ↑c))
      (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0}
        (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} (HPow.hPow.{0, 0, 0} K (13 / 2)) (HPow.hPow.{0, 0, 0} (↑(Nat.card.{u_1} ↑A)) (1 / 2)))
        (HPow.hPow.{0, 0, 0} (↑(Nat.card.{u_1} ↥H)) (-1 / 2))))
    (And (LE.le.{0} (↑(Nat.card.{u_1} ↥H)) (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} (HPow.hPow.{0, 0, 0} K 11) ↑(Nat.card.{u_1} ↑A)))
      (And (LE.le.{0} (↑(Nat.card.{u_1} ↑A)) (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} (HPow.hPow.{0, 0, 0} K 11) ↑(Nat.card.{u_1} ↥H)))
        (HasSubset.Subset.{u_1} A (HAdd.hAdd.{u_1, u_1, u_1} c ↑H))))

result.statement: For $\eta = 1/8$, there exist tau-minimizers $X_1, X_2$ satisfying $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
result.proof: For each $\eta <1/8$, consider minimizers $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ from \Cref{tau-min}. By \Cref{de-prop-improv}, they satisfy $d[X_1^\eta ; X_2^\eta ]=0$. By compactness of the space of probability measures on $G$, one may extract a converging subsequence of the distributions of $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ as $\eta \to 1/8$. By continuity of all the involved quantities, the limit is a pair of tau-minimizers for $1/8$ satisfying additionally $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.

result.statement: For $\eta = 1/8$, there exist tau-minimizers $X_1, X_2$ satisfying $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
result.proof: For each $\eta <1/8$, consider minimizers $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ from \Cref{tau-min}. By \Cref{de-prop-improv}, they satisfy $d[X_1^\eta ; X_2^\eta ]=0$. By compactness of the space of probability measures on $G$, one may extract a converging subsequence of the distributions of $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ as $\eta \to 1/8$. By continuity of all the involved quantities, the limit is a pair of tau-minimizers for $1/8$ satisfying additionally $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.

nodes.claim: For a sequence of pairs of probability measures on a finite discrete G, there is a converging subsequence in the weak topology of ProbabilityMeasure G × ProbabilityMeasure G.
nodes.proof_hint: Use compactness of ProbabilityMeasure G for finite/discrete spaces, or a finite-dimensional closed simplex argument.

nodes.claim: If q n are refPackages with 8*(q n).η<1 and q n → p, and for each n X1n X2n are tau-minimizers for q n with rdist 0, then a subsequence of their probability laws has limits μ,ν; μ,ν are probability laws of measurable functions realizing p.
nodes.proof_hint: Apply P2 to the sequence of law pairs; use continuity of tau and rdist to show the limit laws satisfy tau_minimizes p and rdist 0.

theorem PFR_conjecture (h₀A : A.Nonempty) (hA : Nat.card (A + A) ≤ K * Nat.card A) :
     ∃ (H : Submodule (ZMod 2) G) (c : Set G),
      Nat.card c < 2 * K ^ 12 ∧ Nat.card H ≤ Nat.card A ∧ A ⊆ c + H
declarations.doc:
The polynomial Freiman-Ruzsa (PFR) conjecture: if `A` is a subset of an elementary abelian
2-group of doubling constant at most `K`, then `A` can be covered by at most `2 * K ^ 12` cosets of
a subgroup of cardinality at most `|A|`.

    LE.le.{0} (↑(Nat.card.{u_1} ↑(HAdd.hAdd.{u_1, u_1, u_1} A A))) (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} K ↑(Nat.card.{u_1} ↑A)) →

        And (LT.lt.{0} (↑(Nat.card.{u_1} ↑c)) (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} 2 (HPow.hPow.{0, 0, 0} K 12)))

result.statement: For $\eta = 1/8$, there exist tau-minimizers $X_1, X_2$ satisfying $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
result.proof: For each $\eta <1/8$, consider minimizers $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ from \Cref{tau-min}. By \Cref{de-prop-improv}, they satisfy $d[X_1^\eta ; X_2^\eta ]=0$. By compactness of the space of probability measures on $G$, one may extract a converging subsequence of the distributions of $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ as $\eta \to 1/8$. By continuity of all the involved quantities, the limit is a pair of tau-minimizers for $1/8$ satisfying additionally $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.

nodes.body:
skip
classical
let h := probabilityMeasureHomeoStdSimplex (X := G)
have hc_simplex : CompactSpace (stdSimplex ℝ G) := by
  rw [← isCompact_univ_iff]
  rw [Subtype.isCompact_iff]
  simpa using isCompact_stdSimplex G
have hc : IsCompact (Set.univ : Set (stdSimplex ℝ G)) := isCompact_univ_iff.mpr hc_simplex
have hseq : IsSeqCompact (Set.univ : Set (stdSimplex ℝ G)) := UniformSpace.isCompact_iff_isSeqCompact.mp hc
rcases hseq (x := fun n => h (x n).1) (by intro n; trivial) with ⟨y₁, hy₁_mem, φ₁, hφ₁mono, hy₁⟩
let μ₁ : MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure G := h.symm y₁
have ht1 : Filter.Tendsto (fun n => (x (φ₁ n)).1) Filter.atTop (nhds μ₁) := by
  simpa [μ₁, Function.comp_def] using (h.symm.continuous.tendsto y₁).comp hy₁
rcases hseq (x := fun n => h (x (φ₁ n)).2) (by intro n; trivial) with ⟨y₂, hy₂_mem, φ₂, hφ₂mono, hy₂⟩
let μ₂ : MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure G := h.symm y₂
have ht2 : Filter.Tendsto (fun n => (x (φ₁ (φ₂ n))).2) Filter.atTop (nhds μ₂) := by
  simpa [μ₂, Function.comp_def] using (h.symm.continuous.tendsto y₂).comp hy₂
let φ : ℕ → ℕ := φ₁ ∘ φ₂
have hφmono : StrictMono φ := hφ₁mono.comp hφ₂mono
have ht1' : Filter.Tendsto (fun n => (x (φ n)).1) Filter.atTop (nhds μ₁) := by
  have ht := ht1.comp (StrictMono.tendsto_atTop hφ₂mono)
  simpa [φ, Function.comp_def] using ht
have ht2' : Filter.Tendsto (fun n => (x (φ n)).2) Filter.atTop (nhds μ₂) := by
  simpa [φ, Function.comp_def] using ht2
exact ⟨μ₁, μ₂, φ, hφmono, ht1', ht2'⟩

result.statement: For $\eta = 1/8$, there exist tau-minimizers $X_1, X_2$ satisfying $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
result.proof: For each $\eta <1/8$, consider minimizers $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ from \Cref{tau-min}. By \Cref{de-prop-improv}, they satisfy $d[X_1^\eta ; X_2^\eta ]=0$. By compactness of the space of probability measures on $G$, one may extract a converging subsequence of the distributions of $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ as $\eta \to 1/8$. By continuity of all the involved quantities, the limit is a pair of tau-minimizers for $1/8$ satisfying additionally $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.

result.statement: For $\eta = 1/8$, there exist tau-minimizers $X_1, X_2$ satisfying $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
result.proof: For each $\eta <1/8$, consider minimizers $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ from \Cref{tau-min}. By \Cref{de-prop-improv}, they satisfy $d[X_1^\eta ; X_2^\eta ]=0$. By compactness of the space of probability measures on $G$, one may extract a converging subsequence of the distributions of $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ as $\eta \to 1/8$. By continuity of all the involved quantities, the limit is a pair of tau-minimizers for $1/8$ satisfying additionally $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.

references.label: de-prop-improv
references.name: tau_strictly_decreases'
references.statement: Suppose $0 < \eta < 1/8$. Let $X_1, X_2$ be tau-minimizers. Then $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.

nodes.claim: There is a sequence q : ℕ → refPackage Ω₀₁ Ω₀₂ G with 8*(q n).η < 1 for all n and (q n).η → p.η, using p for the base random variables.
nodes.proof_hint: Set q n.η = p.η*(something below 1) or p.η - 1/n+, preserving X₀₁, X₀₂ and using refPackage constructor.

nodes.claim: For any probability measures μ ν on finite G, there is a probability space Ω and measurable X₁ X₂ on Ω whose laws are μ and ν respectively.
nodes.proof_hint: Take Ω = G × G with the product measure μ.prod ν, X₁ = fst and X₂ = snd, and use projection measurability and probability product instance.

nodes.claim: For any refPackage q with 8 * q.η < 1, there exist measurable probability-space variables X₁, X₂ with tau_minimizes q X₁ X₂ and d[X₁ # X₂] = 0.
nodes.proof_hint: Use tau_minimizer_exists q and tau_strictly_decreases'.

nodes.claim: For a sequence of pairs of probability measures on a finite discrete G, there is a converging subsequence in the weak topology of ProbabilityMeasure G × ProbabilityMeasure G.
nodes.proof_hint: Use compactness of ProbabilityMeasure G for finite/discrete spaces, or a finite-dimensional closed simplex argument.

nodes.claim: If q n are refPackages with 8*(q n).η<1 and q n → p, and for each n X1n X2n are tau-minimizers for q n with rdist 0, then a subsequence of their probability laws has limits μ,ν; μ,ν are probability laws of measurable functions realizing p.
nodes.proof_hint: Apply P2 to the sequence of law pairs; use continuity of tau and rdist to show the limit laws satisfy tau_minimizes p and rdist 0.

nodes.claim: For a sequence of pairs of probability measures on a finite discrete G, there is a converging subsequence in the weak topology of ProbabilityMeasure G × ProbabilityMeasure G.
nodes.body:
skip
classical
let h := probabilityMeasureHomeoStdSimplex (X := G)
have hc_simplex : CompactSpace (stdSimplex ℝ G) := by
  rw [← isCompact_univ_iff]
  rw [Subtype.isCompact_iff]
  simpa using isCompact_stdSimplex G
have hc : IsCompact (Set.univ : Set (stdSimplex ℝ G)) := isCompact_univ_iff.mpr hc_simplex
have hseq : IsSeqCompact (Set.univ : Set (stdSimplex ℝ G)) := UniformSpace.isCompact_iff_isSeqCompact.mp hc
rcases hseq (x := fun n => h (x n).1) (by intro n; trivial) with ⟨y₁, hy₁_mem, φ₁, hφ₁mono, hy₁⟩
let μ₁ : MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure G := h.symm y₁
have ht1 : Filter.Tendsto (fun n => (x (φ₁ n)).1) Filter.atTop (nhds μ₁) := by
  simpa [μ₁, Function.comp_def] using (h.symm.continuous.tendsto y₁).comp hy₁
rcases hseq (x := fun n => h (x (φ₁ n)).2) (by intro n; trivial) with ⟨y₂, hy₂_mem, φ₂, hφ₂mono, hy₂⟩
let μ₂ : MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure G := h.symm y₂
have ht2 : Filter.Tendsto (fun n => (x (φ₁ (φ₂ n))).2) Filter.atTop (nhds μ₂) := by
  simpa [μ₂, Function.comp_def] using (h.symm.continuous.tendsto y₂).comp hy₂
let φ : ℕ → ℕ := φ₁ ∘ φ₂
have hφmono : StrictMono φ := hφ₁mono.comp hφ₂mono
have ht1' : Filter.Tendsto (fun n => (x (φ n)).1) Filter.atTop (nhds μ₁) := by
  have ht := ht1.comp (StrictMono.tendsto_atTop hφ₂mono)
  simpa [φ, Function.comp_def] using ht
have ht2' : Filter.Tendsto (fun n => (x (φ n)).2) Filter.atTop (nhds μ₂) := by
  simpa [φ, Function.comp_def] using ht2
exact ⟨μ₁, μ₂, φ, hφmono, ht1', ht2'⟩

  [inst_2 :

      (@MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume.{u_1} Ω₀₁ inst)]
  [inst_3 :
    @MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure.{u_2} Ω₀₂ (@MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.toMeasurableSpace.{u_2} Ω₀₂ inst_1)
      (@MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume.{u_2} Ω₀₂ inst_1)]
  {G : Type uG} [inst_4 : AddCommGroup.{uG} G]
  [inst_5 :
    @Module.{0, uG} (ZMod (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat 2 (instOfNatNat 2))) G
      (@DivisionSemiring.toSemiring.{0} (ZMod (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat 2 (instOfNatNat 2)))
        (@Semifield.toDivisionSemiring.{0} (ZMod (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat 2 (instOfNatNat 2)))
          (@Field.toSemifield.{0} (ZMod (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat 2 (instOfNatNat 2)))
            (@ZMod.instField (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat 2 (instOfNatNat 2)) Nat.fact_prime_two))))
      (@AddCommGroup.toAddCommMonoid.{uG} G inst_4)]
  [inst_6 : Fintype.{uG} G] [inst_7 : MeasurableSpace.{uG} G] [inst_8 : @MeasurableSingletonClass.{uG} G inst_7]
  (p : @refPackage.{uG, u_1, u_2} Ω₀₁ Ω₀₂ inst inst_1 G inst_7),
  @Exists.{uG + 2} (Type uG) fun (Ω : Type uG) =>
    @Exists.{uG + 1} (MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.{uG} Ω) fun (x : MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.{uG} Ω) =>
      @Exists.{uG + 1} (Ω → G) fun (X₁ : Ω → G) =>
        @Exists.{uG + 1} (Ω → G) fun (X₂ : Ω → G) =>
          And (@Measurable.{uG, uG} Ω G (@MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.toMeasurableSpace.{uG} Ω x) inst_7 X₁)
            (And (@Measurable.{uG, uG} Ω G (@MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.toMeasurableSpace.{uG} Ω x) inst_7 X₂)
              (And
                (@MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure.{uG} Ω (@MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.toMeasurableSpace.{uG} Ω x)
                  (@MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume.{uG} Ω x))
                (And (@tau_minimizes.{uG, u_1, u_2, uG} Ω₀₁ Ω₀₂ inst inst_1 G inst_4 inst_7 p Ω x X₁ X₂)
                  (@Eq.{1} Real
                    (@rdist.{uG, uG, uG} Ω Ω G (@MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.toMeasurableSpace.{uG} Ω x)
                      (@MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.toMeasurableSpace.{uG} Ω x) inst_7 inst_4 X₁ X₂
                      (@MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume.{uG} Ω x) (@MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume.{uG} Ω x))
                    (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Real 0 (@Zero.toOfNat0.{0} Real Real.instZero))))))

declarations.source_snippet:
theorem tendsto_iff_forall_lintegral_tendsto {γ : Type*} {F : Filter γ}
    {μs : γ → ProbabilityMeasure Ω} {μ : ProbabilityMeasure Ω} :
    Tendsto μs F (𝓝 μ) ↔
      ∀ f : Ω →ᵇ ℝ≥0,
        Tendsto (fun i ↦ ∫⁻ ω, f ω ∂(μs i : Measure Ω)) F (𝓝 (∫⁻ ω, f ω ∂(μ : Measure Ω)))
declarations.doc:
A characterization of weak convergence of probability measures by the condition that the
integrals of every continuous bounded nonnegative function converge to the integral of the function
against the limit measure.

The characterization of weak convergence of probability measures by the usual (defining)
condition that the integrals of every continuous bounded function converge to the integral of the
function against the limit measure.

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure.tendsto_map_of_tendsto_of_continuous
declarations.source_snippet:
lemma tendsto_map_of_tendsto_of_continuous {ι : Type*} {L : Filter ι}
    (νs : ι → ProbabilityMeasure Ω) (ν : ProbabilityMeasure Ω) (lim : Tendsto νs L (𝓝 ν))
    {f : Ω → Ω'} (f_cont : Continuous f) :
    Tendsto (fun i ↦ (νs i).map f_cont.measurable.aemeasurable) L
      (𝓝 (ν.map f_cont.measurable.aemeasurable))
declarations.doc:
If `f : X → Y` is continuous and `Y` is equipped with the Borel sigma algebra, then
convergence (in distribution) of `ProbabilityMeasure`s on `X` implies convergence (in
distribution) of the push-forwards of these measures by `f`.

    {E : Set Ω} (E_nullbdry : μ (frontier E) = 0) : Tendsto (fun i ↦ μs i E) L (𝓝 (μ E))
declarations.doc:
One implication of the portmanteau theorem:
Weak convergence of probability measures implies that if the boundary of a Borel set
carries no probability mass under the limit measure, then the limit of the measures of the set
equals the measure of the set under the limit probability measure.

A version with coercions to ordinary `ℝ≥0∞`-valued measures is
`MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure.tendsto_measure_of_null_frontier_of_tendsto'`.

If `f : X → Y` is continuous and `Y` is equipped with the Borel sigma algebra, then
convergence (in distribution) of `ProbabilityMeasure`s on `X` implies convergence (in

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure.tendsto_iff_forall_lintegral_tendsto
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem tendsto_iff_forall_lintegral_tendsto {γ : Type*} {F : Filter γ}
    {μs : γ → ProbabilityMeasure Ω} {μ : ProbabilityMeasure Ω} :
    Tendsto μs F (𝓝 μ) ↔
      ∀ f : Ω →ᵇ ℝ≥0,
        Tendsto (fun i ↦ ∫⁻ ω, f ω ∂(μs i : Measure Ω)) F (𝓝 (∫⁻ ω, f ω ∂(μ : Measure Ω)))
declarations.doc:
A characterization of weak convergence of probability measures by the condition that the
integrals of every continuous bounded nonnegative function converge to the integral of the function
against the limit measure.

declarations.doc:
The characterization of weak convergence of probability measures by the usual (defining)
condition that the integrals of every continuous bounded function converge to the integral of the
function against the limit measure.

theorem tendsto_normalize_iff_tendsto {γ : Type*} {F : Filter γ} {μs : γ → FiniteMeasure Ω}

declarations.doc:
The weak convergence of finite measures to a nonzero limit can be characterized by the weak
convergence of both their normalized versions (probability measures) and their total masses.

declarations.source_snippet:
theorem ProbabilityMeasure.tendsto_measure_of_null_frontier_of_tendsto {Ω ι : Type*} {L : Filter ι}
    [MeasurableSpace Ω] [PseudoEMetricSpace Ω] [OpensMeasurableSpace Ω] [HasOuterApproxClosed Ω]
    {μ : ProbabilityMeasure Ω} {μs : ι → ProbabilityMeasure Ω} (μs_lim : Tendsto μs L (𝓝 μ))
    {E : Set Ω} (E_nullbdry : μ (frontier E) = 0) : Tendsto (fun i ↦ μs i E) L (𝓝 (μ E))
declarations.doc:
One implication of the portmanteau theorem:
Weak convergence of probability measures implies that if the boundary of a Borel set
carries no probability mass under the limit measure, then the limit of the measures of the set
equals the measure of the set under the limit probability measure.

A version with coercions to ordinary `ℝ≥0∞`-valued measures is
`MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure.tendsto_measure_of_null_frontier_of_tendsto'`.

result.statement: For $\eta = 1/8$, there exist tau-minimizers $X_1, X_2$ satisfying $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
result.proof: For each $\eta <1/8$, consider minimizers $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ from \Cref{tau-min}. By \Cref{de-prop-improv}, they satisfy $d[X_1^\eta ; X_2^\eta ]=0$. By compactness of the space of probability measures on $G$, one may extract a converging subsequence of the distributions of $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ as $\eta \to 1/8$. By continuity of all the involved quantities, the limit is a pair of tau-minimizers for $1/8$ satisfying additionally $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure.tendsto_map_of_tendsto_of_continuous
declarations.source_snippet:
lemma tendsto_map_of_tendsto_of_continuous {ι : Type*} {L : Filter ι}
    (νs : ι → ProbabilityMeasure Ω) (ν : ProbabilityMeasure Ω) (lim : Tendsto νs L (𝓝 ν))
    {f : Ω → Ω'} (f_cont : Continuous f) :
    Tendsto (fun i ↦ (νs i).map f_cont.measurable.aemeasurable) L
      (𝓝 (ν.map f_cont.measurable.aemeasurable))
declarations.doc:
If `f : X → Y` is continuous and `Y` is equipped with the Borel sigma algebra, then
convergence (in distribution) of `ProbabilityMeasure`s on `X` implies convergence (in
distribution) of the push-forwards of these measures by `f`.

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure.tendsto_iff_forall_lintegral_tendsto
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem tendsto_iff_forall_lintegral_tendsto {γ : Type*} {F : Filter γ}
    {μs : γ → ProbabilityMeasure Ω} {μ : ProbabilityMeasure Ω} :
    Tendsto μs F (𝓝 μ) ↔
      ∀ f : Ω →ᵇ ℝ≥0,
        Tendsto (fun i ↦ ∫⁻ ω, f ω ∂(μs i : Measure Ω)) F (𝓝 (∫⁻ ω, f ω ∂(μ : Measure Ω)))
declarations.doc:
A characterization of weak convergence of probability measures by the condition that the
integrals of every continuous bounded nonnegative function converge to the integral of the function
against the limit measure.

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure.tendsto_iff_forall_integral_tendsto
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem tendsto_iff_forall_integral_tendsto {γ : Type*} {F : Filter γ}
    {μs : γ → ProbabilityMeasure Ω} {μ : ProbabilityMeasure Ω} :
    Tendsto μs F (𝓝 μ) ↔
      ∀ f : Ω →ᵇ ℝ,
        Tendsto (fun i ↦ ∫ ω, f ω ∂(μs i : Measure Ω)) F (𝓝 (∫ ω, f ω ∂(μ : Measure Ω)))
declarations.doc:
The characterization of weak convergence of probability measures by the usual (defining)
condition that the integrals of every continuous bounded function converge to the integral of the
function against the limit measure.

declarations.name: ent_bsg
declarations.source_snippet:
lemma ent_bsg [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {A B : Ω → G} (hA : Measurable A) (hB : Measurable B)
    [Fintype G] :
    (μ.map (A + B))[fun z ↦ d[A ; μ[|(A + B) ⁻¹' {z}] # B ; μ[|(A + B) ⁻¹' {z}]]]
      ≤ 3 * I[A : B; μ] + 2 * H[A + B ; μ] - H[A ; μ] - H[B ; μ]
declarations.doc:
The **entropic Balog-Szemerédi-Gowers inequality**. Let $A, B$ be $G$-valued random variables on
$\Omega$, and set $Z := A+B$. Then
$$\sum_{z} P[Z=z] d[(A | Z = z) ; (B | Z = z)] \leq 3 I[A :B] + 2 H[Z] - H[A] - H[B]. $$
TODO: remove the hypothesis of `Fintype G` from here and from `condIndep_copies'`

  τ : ℝ
  one_lt_tau : 1 < τ
declarations.doc:
A Besicovitch tau-package is a family of balls in a metric space with positive bounded radii,
together with enough data to proceed with the Besicovitch greedy algorithm. We register this in
a single structure to make sure that all our constructions in this algorithm only depend on
one variable.

theorem lastStep_nonempty :
    {i | ¬∃ b : β, p.c b ∉ p.iUnionUpTo i ∧ p.R i ≤ p.τ * p.r b}.Nonempty

declarations.name: Besicovitch.TauPackage.index
declarations.source_snippet:
noncomputable def index : Ordinal.{u} → β
  | i =>
                                                                               
      let Z := ⋃ j : { j // j < i }, ball (p.c (index j)) (p.r (index j))
                                                                          
      let R := iSup fun b : { b : β // p.c b ∉ Z } => p.r b
                                                                                           
                                                                        
      Classical.epsilon fun b : β => p.c b ∉ Z ∧ R ≤ p.τ * p.r b
  termination_by i => i
  decreasing_by exact j.2
declarations.doc:
Choose inductively large balls with centers that are not contained in the union of already
chosen balls. This is a transfinite induction.

declarations.name: Besicovitch.TauPackage.R
declarations.source_snippet:
def R (i : Ordinal.{u}) : ℝ :=
  iSup fun b : { b : β // p.c b ∉ p.iUnionUpTo i } => p.r b
declarations.doc: Supremum of the radii of balls whose centers are not yet covered at step `i`.

structure TauPackage (β : Type*) (α : Type*) extends BallPackage β α where

declarations.doc:
A Besicovitch tau-package is a family of balls in a metric space with positive bounded radii,
together with enough data to proceed with the Besicovitch greedy algorithm. We register this in
a single structure to make sure that all our constructions in this algorithm only depend on
one variable.

result.statement: For $\eta = 1/8$, there exist tau-minimizers $X_1, X_2$ satisfying $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
result.proof: For each $\eta <1/8$, consider minimizers $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ from \Cref{tau-min}. By \Cref{de-prop-improv}, they satisfy $d[X_1^\eta ; X_2^\eta ]=0$. By compactness of the space of probability measures on $G$, one may extract a converging subsequence of the distributions of $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ as $\eta \to 1/8$. By continuity of all the involved quantities, the limit is a pair of tau-minimizers for $1/8$ satisfying additionally $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.

result.proof: For each $\eta <1/8$, consider minimizers $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ from \Cref{tau-min}. By \Cref{de-prop-improv}, they satisfy $d[X_1^\eta ; X_2^\eta ]=0$. By compactness of the space of probability measures on $G$, one may extract a converging subsequence of the distributions of $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ as $\eta \to 1/8$. By continuity of all the involved quantities, the limit is a pair of tau-minimizers for $1/8$ satisfying additionally $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.

result.statement: For $\eta = 1/8$, there exist tau-minimizers $X_1, X_2$ satisfying $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
result.proof: For each $\eta <1/8$, consider minimizers $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ from \Cref{tau-min}. By \Cref{de-prop-improv}, they satisfy $d[X_1^\eta ; X_2^\eta ]=0$. By compactness of the space of probability measures on $G$, one may extract a converging subsequence of the distributions of $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ as $\eta \to 1/8$. By continuity of all the involved quantities, the limit is a pair of tau-minimizers for $1/8$ satisfying additionally $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.

lemma ent_bsg [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {A B : Ω → G} (hA : Measurable A) (hB : Measurable B)
    [Fintype G] :
    (μ.map (A + B))[fun z ↦ d[A ; μ[|(A + B) ⁻¹' {z}] # B ; μ[|(A + B) ⁻¹' {z}]]]
      ≤ 3 * I[A : B; μ] + 2 * H[A + B ; μ] - H[A ; μ] - H[B ; μ]
declarations.doc:
The **entropic Balog-Szemerédi-Gowers inequality**. Let $A, B$ be $G$-valued random variables on
$\Omega$, and set $Z := A+B$. Then
$$\sum_{z} P[Z=z] d[(A | Z = z) ; (B | Z = z)] \leq 3 I[A :B] + 2 H[Z] - H[A] - H[B]. $$

declarations.name: ProbabilityTheory.IsUniform
declarations.source_snippet:
structure IsUniform (H : Set S) (X : Ω → S) (μ : Measure Ω := by volume_tac) : Prop where
  eq_of_mem ⦃x⦄ (hx : x ∈ H) ⦃y⦄ (hy : y ∈ H) : μ (X ⁻¹' {x}) = μ (X ⁻¹' {y})
  measure_preimage_compl : μ (X ⁻¹' Hᶜ) = 0
declarations.doc:
The assertion that the law of $X$ is the uniform probability measure on a finite set $H$.
While in applications $H$ will be non-empty finite set, $X$ measurable, and and $μ$ a probability
measure, it could be technically convenient to have a definition that works even without these
hypotheses. (For instance, `isUniform` would be well-defined, but false, for infinite `H`).

This should probably be refactored, requiring instead that `μ.map X = uniformOn H`.

declarations.name: ProbabilityTheory.condEntropy
declarations.doc:
Conditional entropy of a random variable w.r.t. another.
This is the expectation under the law of `Y` of the entropy of the law of `X` conditioned on the
event `Y = y`.

    (X₁ : Ω₁ → G) (X₂ : Ω₂ → G) (μ₁ : Measure Ω₁) (μ₂ : Measure Ω₂) : ℝ :=
  d[X₁ ; μ₁ # X₂ ; μ₂] + p.η * d[p.X₀₁ ; ℙ # X₁ ; μ₁] + p.η * d[p.X₀₂ ; ℙ # X₂ ; μ₂]

$$ \tau[X_1; X_2] := d[X_1; X_2] + \eta d[X^0_1; X_1] + \eta d[X^0_2; X_2].$$

We denote it as `τ[X₁ ; μ₁ # X₂ ; μ₂ | p]` where `p` is a fixed package containing the information
of the reference random variables. When the measurable spaces have a canonical measure `ℙ`, we
can use `τ[X₁ # X₂ | p]`

declarations.source_snippet:
noncomputable def probabilityMeasureEquivStdSimplex [Fintype X] [MeasurableSingletonClass X] :
    ProbabilityMeasure X ≃ stdSimplex ℝ X where
  toFun := by
    intro μ
    refine ⟨fun i ↦ (μ {i}).toReal, by simp, ?_⟩
    simp only
    rw [← NNReal.coe_sum, ProbabilityMeasure.coeFn_def,
      ← ENNReal.toNNReal_sum (fun a _ha ↦ by finiteness)]
    simp
  invFun := by
    intro p
    refine ⟨∑ i, ENNReal.ofReal ((p : X → ℝ) i) • Measure.dirac i, ⟨?_⟩⟩
    simp only [Measure.coe_finset_sum, Measure.coe_smul, Finset.sum_apply, Pi.smul_apply,
      measure_univ, smul_eq_mul, mul_one]
    rw [← ENNReal.toReal_eq_toReal (by simp [ENNReal.sum_eq_top]) ENNReal.one_ne_top,
        ENNReal.toReal_sum (by simp)]
    simp_rw [ENNReal.toReal_ofReal (p.2.1 _), p.2.2, ENNReal.one_toReal]
  left_inv := by
    intro μ
    ext s _hs
    conv_rhs => rw [← Measure.sum_smul_dirac (μ := (μ : Measure X))]
    simp
  right_inv := by
    rintro ⟨p, p_pos, hp⟩
    ext i
    simp only [ProbabilityMeasure.mk_apply, Measure.coe_finset_sum, Measure.coe_smul,
      Finset.sum_apply, Pi.smul_apply, MeasurableSet.singleton, Measure.dirac_apply', smul_eq_mul]
    rw [Finset.sum_eq_single_of_mem i (Finset.mem_univ i)]
    · simp only [Measure.smul_apply, MeasurableSet.singleton, Measure.dirac_apply',
        Set.mem_singleton_iff, Set.indicator_of_mem, Pi.one_apply, smul_eq_mul, mul_one]
      exact ENNReal.toReal_ofReal (p_pos i)
    · intro b _ bi
      simp [bi]

declarations.name: exists_norm_eq_iInf_of_complete_convex
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem exists_norm_eq_iInf_of_complete_convex {K : Set F} (ne : K.Nonempty) (h₁ : IsComplete K)
    (h₂ : Convex ℝ K) : ∀ u : F, ∃ v ∈ K, ‖u - v‖ = ⨅ w : K, ‖u - w‖
declarations.doc:
Existence of minimizers
Let `u` be a point in a real inner product space, and let `K` be a nonempty complete convex subset.
Then there exists a (unique) `v` in `K` that minimizes the distance `‖u - v‖` to `u`.

declarations.name: norm_eq_iInf_iff_inner_eq_zero
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem norm_eq_iInf_iff_inner_eq_zero {u : E} {v : E} (hv : v ∈ K) :
    (‖u - v‖ = ⨅ w : K, ‖u - w‖) ↔ ∀ w ∈ K, ⟪u - v, w⟫ = 0
declarations.doc:
Characterization of minimizers in the projection on a subspace.
Let `u` be a point in an inner product space, and let `K` be a nonempty subspace.
Then point `v` minimizes the distance `‖u - v‖` over points in `K` if and only if
for all `w ∈ K`, `⟪u - v, w⟫ = 0` (i.e., `u - v` is orthogonal to the subspace `K`)

declarations.name: norm_eq_iInf_iff_real_inner_eq_zero
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem norm_eq_iInf_iff_real_inner_eq_zero (K : Submodule ℝ F) {u : F} {v : F} (hv : v ∈ K) :
    (‖u - v‖ = ⨅ w : (↑K : Set F), ‖u - w‖) ↔ ∀ w ∈ K, ⟪u - v, w⟫_ℝ = 0
declarations.doc:
Characterization of minimizers in the projection on a subspace, in the real case.
Let `u` be a point in a real inner product space, and let `K` be a nonempty subspace.
Then point `v` minimizes the distance `‖u - v‖` over points in `K` if and only if
for all `w ∈ K`, `⟪u - v, w⟫ = 0` (i.e., `u - v` is orthogonal to the subspace `K`).
This is superseded by `norm_eq_iInf_iff_inner_eq_zero` that gives the same conclusion over
any `RCLike` field.

declarations.name: ProbabilityTheory.IsUniform
declarations.source_snippet:
structure IsUniform (H : Set S) (X : Ω → S) (μ : Measure Ω := by volume_tac) : Prop where
  eq_of_mem ⦃x⦄ (hx : x ∈ H) ⦃y⦄ (hy : y ∈ H) : μ (X ⁻¹' {x}) = μ (X ⁻¹' {y})
  measure_preimage_compl : μ (X ⁻¹' Hᶜ) = 0
declarations.doc:
The assertion that the law of $X$ is the uniform probability measure on a finite set $H$.
While in applications $H$ will be non-empty finite set, $X$ measurable, and and $μ$ a probability
measure, it could be technically convenient to have a definition that works even without these
hypotheses. (For instance, `isUniform` would be well-defined, but false, for infinite `H`).

This should probably be refactored, requiring instead that `μ.map X = uniformOn H`.
