declarations.name: ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun
declarations.doc:
A family of functions defined on the same space `Ω` and taking values in possibly different
spaces, each with a measurable space structure, is independent if the family of measurable space
structures they generate on `Ω` is independent. For a function `g` with codomain having measurable
space structure `m`, the generated measurable space structure is `MeasurableSpace.comap g m`.

declarations.name: ProbabilityTheory.iCondIndepFun
declarations.doc:
A family of functions defined on the same space `Ω` and taking values in possibly different
spaces, each with a measurable space structure, is conditionally independent if the family of
measurable space structures they generate on `Ω` is conditionally independent. For a function `g`
with codomain having measurable space structure `m`, the generated measurable space structure is
`m.comap g`.
See `ProbabilityTheory.iCondIndepFun_iff`.

declarations.name: ProbabilityTheory.Kernel.iIndepFun
declarations.source_snippet:
def iIndepFun {_mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {β : ι → Type*} (m : ∀ x : ι, MeasurableSpace (β x))
    (f : ∀ x : ι, Ω → β x) (κ : Kernel α Ω)
    (μ : Measure α := by volume_tac) : Prop :=
  iIndep (fun x ↦ MeasurableSpace.comap (f x) (m x)) κ μ
declarations.doc:
A family of functions defined on the same space `Ω` and taking values in possibly different

space structure `m`, the generated measurable space structure is `MeasurableSpace.comap g m`.

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.HasPDF
declarations.source_snippet:
class HasPDF {m : MeasurableSpace Ω} (X : Ω → E) (ℙ : Measure Ω) (μ : Measure E := by volume_tac) :
    Prop where
  protected aemeasurable' : AEMeasurable X ℙ
  protected haveLebesgueDecomposition' : (map X ℙ).HaveLebesgueDecomposition μ
  protected absolutelyContinuous' : map X ℙ ≪ μ
declarations.doc:
A random variable `X : Ω → E` is said to have a probability density function (`HasPDF`)
with respect to the measure `ℙ` on `Ω` and `μ` on `E`
if the push-forward measure of `ℙ` along `X` is absolutely continuous with respect to `μ`
and they have a Lebesgue decomposition (`HaveLebesgueDecomposition`).

result.statement: For $\eta = 1/8$, there exist tau-minimizers $X_1, X_2$ satisfying $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
result.proof: For each $\eta <1/8$, consider minimizers $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ from \Cref{tau-min}. By \Cref{de-prop-improv}, they satisfy $d[X_1^\eta ; X_2^\eta ]=0$. By compactness of the space of probability measures on $G$, one may extract a converging subsequence of the distributions of $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ as $\eta \to 1/8$. By continuity of all the involved quantities, the limit is a pair of tau-minimizers for $1/8$ satisfying additionally $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.

declarations.name: ProbabilityTheory.independent_copies_two
declarations.source_snippet:
lemma independent_copies_two {Ω : Type u} {Ω' : Type v} [MeasureSpace Ω] [MeasureSpace Ω']
    [IsProbabilityMeasure (ℙ : Measure Ω)] [IsProbabilityMeasure (ℙ : Measure Ω')]
    {X : Ω → α} {Y : Ω' → β} (hX : Measurable X) (hY : Measurable Y) :
    ∃ (Ω'' : Type (max u v)) (m'' : MeasureSpace Ω'') (X' : Ω'' → α) (Y' : Ω'' → β),
    IsProbabilityMeasure (ℙ : Measure Ω'') ∧ Measurable X' ∧ Measurable Y' ∧
      IndepFun X' Y' ∧ IdentDistrib X' X ∧ IdentDistrib Y' Y
declarations.doc:
For `X, Y` random variables, one can find independent copies `X', Y'` of `X, Y`. Version
formulated in spaces with a canonical measures.
declarations.type:
∀ {α : Type u_7} {β : Type u_9} [inst : MeasurableSpace.{u_7} α] [inst_1 : MeasurableSpace.{u_9} β] {Ω : Type u}
  {Ω' : Type v} [inst_2 : MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.{u} Ω] [inst_3 : MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.{v} Ω']
  [inst_4 : MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure.{u} MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume.{u}]
  [inst_5 : MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure.{v} MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume.{v}] {X : Ω → α} {Y : Ω' → β},
  Measurable.{u, u_7} X →
    Measurable.{v, u_9} Y →
      ∃ Ω'' m'' X' Y',
        And (MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure.{max u v} MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume.{max u v})
          (And (Measurable.{max u v, u_7} X')
            (And (Measurable.{max u v, u_9} Y')
              (And (ProbabilityTheory.IndepFun.{max u v, u_7, u_9} X' Y' MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume.{max u v})
                (And
                  (ProbabilityTheory.IdentDistrib.{max u v, u, u_7} X' X MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume.{max u v}
                    MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume.{u})
                  (ProbabilityTheory.IdentDistrib.{max u v, v, u_9} Y' Y MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume.{max u v}
                    MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume.{v})))))
declarations.conclusion:
∃ Ω'' m'' X' Y',
  And (MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure.{max u v} MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume.{max u v})
    (And (Measurable.{max u v, u_7} X')
      (And (Measurable.{max u v, u_9} Y')
        (And (ProbabilityTheory.IndepFun.{max u v, u_7, u_9} X' Y' MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume.{max u v})
          (And
            (ProbabilityTheory.IdentDistrib.{max u v, u, u_7} X' X MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume.{max u v}

            (ProbabilityTheory.IdentDistrib.{max u v, v, u_9} Y' Y MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume.{max u v}
              MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume.{v})))))

result.statement: For $\eta = 1/8$, there exist tau-minimizers $X_1, X_2$ satisfying $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
result.proof: For each $\eta <1/8$, consider minimizers $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ from \Cref{tau-min}. By \Cref{de-prop-improv}, they satisfy $d[X_1^\eta ; X_2^\eta ]=0$. By compactness of the space of probability measures on $G$, one may extract a converging subsequence of the distributions of $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ as $\eta \to 1/8$. By continuity of all the involved quantities, the limit is a pair of tau-minimizers for $1/8$ satisfying additionally $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.

nodes.claim: For any probability measures μ ν on finite G, there is a probability space Ω and measurable X₁ X₂ on Ω whose laws are μ and ν respectively.
nodes.proof_hint: Take Ω = G × G with the product measure μ.prod ν, X₁ = fst and X₂ = snd, and use projection measurability and probability product instance.

nodes.claim: For a sequence of pairs of probability measures on a finite discrete G, there is a converging subsequence in the weak topology of ProbabilityMeasure G × ProbabilityMeasure G.
nodes.proof_hint: Use compactness of ProbabilityMeasure G for finite/discrete spaces, or a finite-dimensional closed simplex argument.

result.statement: For $\eta = 1/8$, there exist tau-minimizers $X_1, X_2$ satisfying $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
result.proof: For each $\eta <1/8$, consider minimizers $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ from \Cref{tau-min}. By \Cref{de-prop-improv}, they satisfy $d[X_1^\eta ; X_2^\eta ]=0$. By compactness of the space of probability measures on $G$, one may extract a converging subsequence of the distributions of $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ as $\eta \to 1/8$. By continuity of all the involved quantities, the limit is a pair of tau-minimizers for $1/8$ satisfying additionally $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.

nodes.claim: For any probability measures μ ν on finite G, there is a probability space Ω and measurable X₁ X₂ on Ω whose laws are μ and ν respectively.
nodes.proof_hint: Take Ω = G × G with the product measure μ.prod ν, X₁ = fst and X₂ = snd, and use projection measurability and probability product instance.

nodes.claim: For any refPackage q with 8 * q.η < 1, there exist measurable probability-space variables X₁, X₂ with tau_minimizes q X₁ X₂ and d[X₁ # X₂] = 0.
nodes.proof_hint: Use tau_minimizer_exists q and tau_strictly_decreases'.

nodes.claim: For a sequence of pairs of probability measures on a finite discrete G, there is a converging subsequence in the weak topology of ProbabilityMeasure G × ProbabilityMeasure G.
nodes.proof_hint: Use compactness of ProbabilityMeasure G for finite/discrete spaces, or a finite-dimensional closed simplex argument.

declarations.source_snippet:
structure TauPackage (β : Type*) (α : Type*) extends BallPackage β α where
  τ : ℝ
  one_lt_tau : 1 < τ
declarations.doc:
A Besicovitch tau-package is a family of balls in a metric space with positive bounded radii,
together with enough data to proceed with the Besicovitch greedy algorithm. We register this in
a single structure to make sure that all our constructions in this algorithm only depend on
one variable.

declarations.name: Besicovitch.TauPackage.iUnionUpTo

  ⋃ j : { j // j < i }, ball (p.c (p.index j)) (p.r (p.index j))
declarations.doc: The set of points that are covered by the union of balls selected at steps `< i`.

declarations.source_snippet:
noncomputable def tau {Ω₁ Ω₂ : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω₁] [MeasurableSpace Ω₂]
    (X₁ : Ω₁ → G) (X₂ : Ω₂ → G) (μ₁ : Measure Ω₁) (μ₂ : Measure Ω₂) : ℝ :=
  d[X₁ ; μ₁ # X₂ ; μ₂] + p.η * d[p.X₀₁ ; ℙ # X₁ ; μ₁] + p.η * d[p.X₀₂ ; ℙ # X₂ ; μ₂]

notation3:max "τ[" X₁ " ; " μ₁ " # " X₂ " ; " μ₂ " | " p"]" => tau p X₁ X₂ μ₁ μ₂

@[inherit_doc tau]
notation3:max "τ[" X₁ " # " X₂ " | " p"]" => tau p X₁ X₂ MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume
declarations.doc:
If $X_1,X_2$ are two $G$-valued random variables, then
$$ \tau[X_1; X_2] := d[X_1; X_2] + \eta d[X^0_1; X_1] + \eta d[X^0_2; X_2].$$
Here, $X^0_1$ and $X^0_2$ are two random variables fixed once and for all in most of the argument.
To lighten notation, We package `X^0_1` and `X^0_2` in a single object named `p`.

We denote it as `τ[X₁ ; μ₁ # X₂ ; μ₂ | p]` where `p` is a fixed package containing the information
of the reference random variables. When the measurable spaces have a canonical measure `ℙ`, we
can use `τ[X₁ # X₂ | p]`

/-- If $X_1,X_2$ are two $G$-valued random variables, then
$$ \tau[X_1; X_2] := d[X_1; X_2] + \eta d[X^0_1; X_1] + \eta d[X^0_2; X_2].$$
Here, $X^0_1$ and $X^0_2$ are two random variables fixed once and for all in most of the argument.
To lighten notation, We package `X^0_1` and `X^0_2` in a single object named `p`.

We denote it as `τ[X₁ ; μ₁ # X₂ ; μ₂ | p]` where `p` is a fixed package containing the information
of the reference random variables. When the measurable spaces have a canonical measure `ℙ`, we
can use `τ[X₁ # X₂ | p]`
-/
declarations.doc:
A structure that packages all the fixed information in the main argument. In this way, when
defining the τ functional, we will only only need to refer to the package once in the notation
instead of stating the reference spaces, the reference measures and the reference random
variables.

The η parameter has now been incorporated into the package, in preparation for being able to
manipulate the package.

  τ : ℝ

declarations.doc:
A Besicovitch tau-package is a family of balls in a metric space with positive bounded radii,
together with enough data to proceed with the Besicovitch greedy algorithm. We register this in
a single structure to make sure that all our constructions in this algorithm only depend on
one variable.

result.statement: For $\eta = 1/8$, there exist tau-minimizers $X_1, X_2$ satisfying $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
result.proof: For each $\eta <1/8$, consider minimizers $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ from \Cref{tau-min}. By \Cref{de-prop-improv}, they satisfy $d[X_1^\eta ; X_2^\eta ]=0$. By compactness of the space of probability measures on $G$, one may extract a converging subsequence of the distributions of $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ as $\eta \to 1/8$. By continuity of all the involved quantities, the limit is a pair of tau-minimizers for $1/8$ satisfying additionally $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.

declarations.doc:
If $X_1,X_2$ are two $G$-valued random variables, then
$$ \tau[X_1; X_2] := d[X_1; X_2] + \eta d[X^0_1; X_1] + \eta d[X^0_2; X_2].$$
Here, $X^0_1$ and $X^0_2$ are two random variables fixed once and for all in most of the argument.
To lighten notation, We package `X^0_1` and `X^0_2` in a single object named `p`.

We denote it as `τ[X₁ ; μ₁ # X₂ ; μ₂ | p]` where `p` is a fixed package containing the information
of the reference random variables. When the measurable spaces have a canonical measure `ℙ`, we
can use `τ[X₁ # X₂ | p]`

result.statement: For $\eta = 1/8$, there exist tau-minimizers $X_1, X_2$ satisfying $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
result.proof: For each $\eta <1/8$, consider minimizers $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ from \Cref{tau-min}. By \Cref{de-prop-improv}, they satisfy $d[X_1^\eta ; X_2^\eta ]=0$. By compactness of the space of probability measures on $G$, one may extract a converging subsequence of the distributions of $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ as $\eta \to 1/8$. By continuity of all the involved quantities, the limit is a pair of tau-minimizers for $1/8$ satisfying additionally $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.

result.statement: For $\eta = 1/8$, there exist tau-minimizers $X_1, X_2$ satisfying $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
result.proof: For each $\eta <1/8$, consider minimizers $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ from \Cref{tau-min}. By \Cref{de-prop-improv}, they satisfy $d[X_1^\eta ; X_2^\eta ]=0$. By compactness of the space of probability measures on $G$, one may extract a converging subsequence of the distributions of $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ as $\eta \to 1/8$. By continuity of all the involved quantities, the limit is a pair of tau-minimizers for $1/8$ satisfying additionally $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.

  generalize (∑' n : ℕ, 1 / (n + 1 : ℝ) ^ s) = Z

lemma tendsto_map_of_tendsto_of_continuous {ι : Type*} {L : Filter ι}

convergence (in distribution) of `ProbabilityMeasure`s on `X` implies convergence (in

declarations.name: tau
declarations.source_snippet:
noncomputable def tau {Ω₁ Ω₂ : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω₁] [MeasurableSpace Ω₂]
    (X₁ : Ω₁ → G) (X₂ : Ω₂ → G) (μ₁ : Measure Ω₁) (μ₂ : Measure Ω₂) : ℝ :=
  d[X₁ ; μ₁ # X₂ ; μ₂] + p.η * d[p.X₀₁ ; ℙ # X₁ ; μ₁] + p.η * d[p.X₀₂ ; ℙ # X₂ ; μ₂]

@[inherit_doc tau]
notation3:max "τ[" X₁ " ; " μ₁ " # " X₂ " ; " μ₂ " | " p"]" => tau p X₁ X₂ μ₁ μ₂

@[inherit_doc tau]
notation3:max "τ[" X₁ " # " X₂ " | " p"]" => tau p X₁ X₂ MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume
declarations.doc:
If $X_1,X_2$ are two $G$-valued random variables, then
$$ \tau[X_1; X_2] := d[X_1; X_2] + \eta d[X^0_1; X_1] + \eta d[X^0_2; X_2].$$
Here, $X^0_1$ and $X^0_2$ are two random variables fixed once and for all in most of the argument.
To lighten notation, We package `X^0_1` and `X^0_2` in a single object named `p`.

We denote it as `τ[X₁ ; μ₁ # X₂ ; μ₂ | p]` where `p` is a fixed package containing the information
of the reference random variables. When the measurable spaces have a canonical measure `ℙ`, we
can use `τ[X₁ # X₂ | p]`

references.name: tau_strictly_decreases'
references.statement: Suppose $0 < \eta < 1/8$. Let $X_1, X_2$ be tau-minimizers. Then $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.

nodes.claim: There is a sequence q : ℕ → refPackage Ω₀₁ Ω₀₂ G with 8*(q n).η < 1 for all n and (q n).η → p.η, using p for the base random variables.
nodes.proof_hint: Set q n.η = p.η*(something below 1) or p.η - 1/n+, preserving X₀₁, X₀₂ and using refPackage constructor.

nodes.claim: For any probability measures μ ν on finite G, there is a probability space Ω and measurable X₁ X₂ on Ω whose laws are μ and ν respectively.
nodes.proof_hint: Take Ω = G × G with the product measure μ.prod ν, X₁ = fst and X₂ = snd, and use projection measurability and probability product instance.

nodes.claim: For any refPackage q with 8 * q.η < 1, there exist measurable probability-space variables X₁, X₂ with tau_minimizes q X₁ X₂ and d[X₁ # X₂] = 0.
nodes.proof_hint: Use tau_minimizer_exists q and tau_strictly_decreases'.

nodes.claim: For a sequence of pairs of probability measures on a finite discrete G, there is a converging subsequence in the weak topology of ProbabilityMeasure G × ProbabilityMeasure G.
nodes.proof_hint: Use compactness of ProbabilityMeasure G for finite/discrete spaces, or a finite-dimensional closed simplex argument.

nodes.claim: If q n are refPackages with 8*(q n).η<1 and q n → p, and for each n X1n X2n are tau-minimizers for q n with rdist 0, then a subsequence of their probability laws has limits μ,ν; μ,ν are probability laws of measurable functions realizing p.
nodes.proof_hint: Apply P2 to the sequence of law pairs; use continuity of tau and rdist to show the limit laws satisfy tau_minimizes p and rdist 0.

lemma ProofSteps.P2.{uG}

    [TopologicalSpace G] [DiscreteTopology G] [BorelSpace G] [OpensMeasurableSpace G]

        Filter.Tendsto (fun n => (x (φ n)).1) Filter.atTop (nhds μ) ∧
        Filter.Tendsto (fun n => (x (φ n)).2) Filter.atTop (nhds ν)

result.proof: For each $\eta <1/8$, consider minimizers $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ from \Cref{tau-min}. By \Cref{de-prop-improv}, they satisfy $d[X_1^\eta ; X_2^\eta ]=0$. By compactness of the space of probability measures on $G$, one may extract a converging subsequence of the distributions of $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ as $\eta \to 1/8$. By continuity of all the involved quantities, the limit is a pair of tau-minimizers for $1/8$ satisfying additionally $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.

result.statement: For $\eta = 1/8$, there exist tau-minimizers $X_1, X_2$ satisfying $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
result.proof: For each $\eta <1/8$, consider minimizers $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ from \Cref{tau-min}. By \Cref{de-prop-improv}, they satisfy $d[X_1^\eta ; X_2^\eta ]=0$. By compactness of the space of probability measures on $G$, one may extract a converging subsequence of the distributions of $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ as $\eta \to 1/8$. By continuity of all the involved quantities, the limit is a pair of tau-minimizers for $1/8$ satisfying additionally $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.

nodes.claim: For a sequence of pairs of probability measures on a finite discrete G, there is a converging subsequence in the weak topology of ProbabilityMeasure G × ProbabilityMeasure G.

result.statement: For $\eta = 1/8$, there exist tau-minimizers $X_1, X_2$ satisfying $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
result.proof: For each $\eta <1/8$, consider minimizers $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ from \Cref{tau-min}. By \Cref{de-prop-improv}, they satisfy $d[X_1^\eta ; X_2^\eta ]=0$. By compactness of the space of probability measures on $G$, one may extract a converging subsequence of the distributions of $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ as $\eta \to 1/8$. By continuity of all the involved quantities, the limit is a pair of tau-minimizers for $1/8$ satisfying additionally $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.

result.statement: For $\eta = 1/8$, there exist tau-minimizers $X_1, X_2$ satisfying $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
result.proof: For each $\eta <1/8$, consider minimizers $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ from \Cref{tau-min}. By \Cref{de-prop-improv}, they satisfy $d[X_1^\eta ; X_2^\eta ]=0$. By compactness of the space of probability measures on $G$, one may extract a converging subsequence of the distributions of $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ as $\eta \to 1/8$. By continuity of all the involved quantities, the limit is a pair of tau-minimizers for $1/8$ satisfying additionally $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.

    Tendsto (fun i ↦ (νs i).map f_cont.measurable.aemeasurable) L
      (𝓝 (ν.map f_cont.measurable.aemeasurable))
declarations.doc:
If `f : X → Y` is continuous and `Y` is equipped with the Borel sigma algebra, then
convergence (in distribution) of `ProbabilityMeasure`s on `X` implies convergence (in
distribution) of the push-forwards of these measures by `f`.

theorem tendsto_iff_forall_lintegral_tendsto {γ : Type*} {F : Filter γ}

      ∀ f : Ω →ᵇ ℝ≥0,
        Tendsto (fun i ↦ ∫⁻ ω, f ω ∂(μs i : Measure Ω)) F (𝓝 (∫⁻ ω, f ω ∂(μ : Measure Ω)))
declarations.doc:
A characterization of weak convergence of probability measures by the condition that the
integrals of every continuous bounded nonnegative function converge to the integral of the function
against the limit measure.

declarations.doc:
The characterization of weak convergence of probability measures by the usual (defining)
condition that the integrals of every continuous bounded function converge to the integral of the
function against the limit measure.

declarations.name: ProbabilityTheory.condEntropy

theorem integral_pdf_smul [IsFiniteMeasure ℙ] {X : Ω → E} [HasPDF X ℙ μ] {f : E → F}
    (hf : AEStronglyMeasurable f μ) : ∫ x, (pdf X ℙ μ x).toReal • f x ∂μ = ∫ x, f (X x) ∂ℙ
declarations.doc:

function `f`, `f ∘ X` is a random variable with expectation `∫ x, pdf X x • f x ∂μ`
where `μ` is a measure on the codomain of `X`.

result.statement: For $\eta = 1/8$, there exist tau-minimizers $X_1, X_2$ satisfying $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
result.proof: For each $\eta <1/8$, consider minimizers $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ from \Cref{tau-min}. By \Cref{de-prop-improv}, they satisfy $d[X_1^\eta ; X_2^\eta ]=0$. By compactness of the space of probability measures on $G$, one may extract a converging subsequence of the distributions of $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ as $\eta \to 1/8$. By continuity of all the involved quantities, the limit is a pair of tau-minimizers for $1/8$ satisfying additionally $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.

result.statement: For $\eta = 1/8$, there exist tau-minimizers $X_1, X_2$ satisfying $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
result.proof: For each $\eta <1/8$, consider minimizers $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ from \Cref{tau-min}. By \Cref{de-prop-improv}, they satisfy $d[X_1^\eta ; X_2^\eta ]=0$. By compactness of the space of probability measures on $G$, one may extract a converging subsequence of the distributions of $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ as $\eta \to 1/8$. By continuity of all the involved quantities, the limit is a pair of tau-minimizers for $1/8$ satisfying additionally $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure.tendsto_iff_forall_lintegral_tendsto
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem tendsto_iff_forall_lintegral_tendsto {γ : Type*} {F : Filter γ}
    {μs : γ → ProbabilityMeasure Ω} {μ : ProbabilityMeasure Ω} :
    Tendsto μs F (𝓝 μ) ↔
      ∀ f : Ω →ᵇ ℝ≥0,
        Tendsto (fun i ↦ ∫⁻ ω, f ω ∂(μs i : Measure Ω)) F (𝓝 (∫⁻ ω, f ω ∂(μ : Measure Ω)))
declarations.doc:
A characterization of weak convergence of probability measures by the condition that the
integrals of every continuous bounded nonnegative function converge to the integral of the function
against the limit measure.

declarations.doc:
The characterization of weak convergence of probability measures by the usual (defining)
condition that the integrals of every continuous bounded function converge to the integral of the
function against the limit measure.

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure.tendsto_measure_of_null_frontier_of_tendsto
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem ProbabilityMeasure.tendsto_measure_of_null_frontier_of_tendsto {Ω ι : Type*} {L : Filter ι}
    [MeasurableSpace Ω] [PseudoEMetricSpace Ω] [OpensMeasurableSpace Ω] [HasOuterApproxClosed Ω]
    {μ : ProbabilityMeasure Ω} {μs : ι → ProbabilityMeasure Ω} (μs_lim : Tendsto μs L (𝓝 μ))
    {E : Set Ω} (E_nullbdry : μ (frontier E) = 0) : Tendsto (fun i ↦ μs i E) L (𝓝 (μ E))
declarations.doc:
One implication of the portmanteau theorem:
Weak convergence of probability measures implies that if the boundary of a Borel set
carries no probability mass under the limit measure, then the limit of the measures of the set
equals the measure of the set under the limit probability measure.

A version with coercions to ordinary `ℝ≥0∞`-valued measures is
`MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure.tendsto_measure_of_null_frontier_of_tendsto'`.

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure.tendsto_map_of_tendsto_of_continuous
declarations.source_snippet:
lemma tendsto_map_of_tendsto_of_continuous {ι : Type*} {L : Filter ι}
    (νs : ι → ProbabilityMeasure Ω) (ν : ProbabilityMeasure Ω) (lim : Tendsto νs L (𝓝 ν))
    {f : Ω → Ω'} (f_cont : Continuous f) :
    Tendsto (fun i ↦ (νs i).map f_cont.measurable.aemeasurable) L
      (𝓝 (ν.map f_cont.measurable.aemeasurable))
declarations.doc:
If `f : X → Y` is continuous and `Y` is equipped with the Borel sigma algebra, then
convergence (in distribution) of `ProbabilityMeasure`s on `X` implies convergence (in
distribution) of the push-forwards of these measures by `f`.

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.tendsto_measure_of_null_frontier
declarations.doc:
One implication of the portmanteau theorem:
For a sequence of Borel probability measures, if the liminf of the measures of any open set is at
least the measure of the open set under a candidate limit measure, then for any set whose
boundary carries no probability mass under the candidate limit measure, then its measures under the
sequence converge to its measure under the candidate limit measure.

declarations.name: refPackage
declarations.source_snippet:
structure refPackage where
  /-- The first variable in a package. -/
  X₀₁ : Ω₀₁ → G
  /-- The second variable in a package. -/
  X₀₂ : Ω₀₂ → G
  hmeas1 : Measurable X₀₁
  hmeas2 : Measurable X₀₂
  /-- The constant that parameterizes how good the package is. The argument only works for
  small enough `η`, typically `≤ 1/9` or `< 1/8`. -/
  η : ℝ
  hη : 0 < η

  τ : ℝ

declarations.doc:
A Besicovitch tau-package is a family of balls in a metric space with positive bounded radii,
together with enough data to proceed with the Besicovitch greedy algorithm. We register this in
a single structure to make sure that all our constructions in this algorithm only depend on
one variable.

structure TauPackage (β : Type*) (α : Type*) extends BallPackage β α where
  τ : ℝ

declarations.doc:
A Besicovitch tau-package is a family of balls in a metric space with positive bounded radii,
together with enough data to proceed with the Besicovitch greedy algorithm. We register this in
a single structure to make sure that all our constructions in this algorithm only depend on
one variable.

result.statement: For $\eta = 1/8$, there exist tau-minimizers $X_1, X_2$ satisfying $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
result.proof: For each $\eta <1/8$, consider minimizers $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ from \Cref{tau-min}. By \Cref{de-prop-improv}, they satisfy $d[X_1^\eta ; X_2^\eta ]=0$. By compactness of the space of probability measures on $G$, one may extract a converging subsequence of the distributions of $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ as $\eta \to 1/8$. By continuity of all the involved quantities, the limit is a pair of tau-minimizers for $1/8$ satisfying additionally $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.

A structure that packages all the fixed information in the main argument. In this way, when
defining the τ functional, we will only only need to refer to the package once in the notation
instead of stating the reference spaces, the reference measures and the reference random
variables.

manipulate the package.

declarations.name: Simps.headStructureEtaReduce
declarations.source_snippet:
partial def headStructureEtaReduce (e : Expr) : MetaM Expr := do
  let env ← getEnv
  let (ctor, args) := e.getAppFnArgs
  let some (.ctorInfo { induct := struct, numParams, ..}) := env.find? ctor | pure e
  let some { fieldNames, .. } := getStructureInfo? env struct | pure e
  let (params, fields) := args.toList.splitAt numParams                                            
  trace[simps.debug]
    "rhs is constructor application with params{indentD params}\nand fields {indentD fields}"
  let field0 :: fieldsTail := fields | return e
  let fieldName0 :: fieldNamesTail := fieldNames.toList | return e
  let (fn0, fieldArgs0) := field0.getAppFnArgs
  unless fn0 == struct ++ fieldName0 do
    trace[simps.debug] "{fn0} ≠ {struct ++ fieldName0}"
    return e
  let (params', reduct :: _) := fieldArgs0.toList.splitAt numParams | unreachable!
  unless params' == params do
    trace[simps.debug] "{params'} ≠ {params}"
    return e
  trace[simps.debug] "Potential structure-eta-reduct:{indentExpr e}\nto{indentExpr reduct}"
  let allArgs := params.toArray.push reduct
  let isEta ← (fieldsTail.zip fieldNamesTail).allM fun (field, fieldName) ↦
    if field.getAppFnArgs == (struct ++ fieldName, allArgs) then pure true else isProof field
  unless isEta do return e
  trace[simps.debug] "Structure-eta-reduce:{indentExpr e}\nto{indentExpr reduct}"
  headStructureEtaReduce reduct
declarations.doc:
Perform head-structure-eta-reduction on expression `e`. That is, if `e` is of the form
`⟨f.1, f.2, ..., f.n⟩` with `f` definitionally equal to `e`, then
`headStructureEtaReduce e = headStructureEtaReduce f` and `headStructureEtaReduce e = e` otherwise.

declarations.source_snippet:
noncomputable def probabilityMeasureEquivStdSimplex [Fintype X] [MeasurableSingletonClass X] :
    ProbabilityMeasure X ≃ stdSimplex ℝ X where
  toFun := by
    intro μ
    refine ⟨fun i ↦ (μ {i}).toReal, by simp, ?_⟩
    simp only
    rw [← NNReal.coe_sum, ProbabilityMeasure.coeFn_def,
      ← ENNReal.toNNReal_sum (fun a _ha ↦ by finiteness)]
    simp
  invFun := by
    intro p
    refine ⟨∑ i, ENNReal.ofReal ((p : X → ℝ) i) • Measure.dirac i, ⟨?_⟩⟩
    simp only [Measure.coe_finset_sum, Measure.coe_smul, Finset.sum_apply, Pi.smul_apply,
      measure_univ, smul_eq_mul, mul_one]
    rw [← ENNReal.toReal_eq_toReal (by simp [ENNReal.sum_eq_top]) ENNReal.one_ne_top,
        ENNReal.toReal_sum (by simp)]
    simp_rw [ENNReal.toReal_ofReal (p.2.1 _), p.2.2, ENNReal.one_toReal]
  left_inv := by
    intro μ
    ext s _hs
    conv_rhs => rw [← Measure.sum_smul_dirac (μ := (μ : Measure X))]
    simp
  right_inv := by
    rintro ⟨p, p_pos, hp⟩
    ext i
    simp only [ProbabilityMeasure.mk_apply, Measure.coe_finset_sum, Measure.coe_smul,
      Finset.sum_apply, Pi.smul_apply, MeasurableSet.singleton, Measure.dirac_apply', smul_eq_mul]
    rw [Finset.sum_eq_single_of_mem i (Finset.mem_univ i)]
    · simp only [Measure.smul_apply, MeasurableSet.singleton, Measure.dirac_apply',
        Set.mem_singleton_iff, Set.indicator_of_mem, Pi.one_apply, smul_eq_mul, mul_one]
      exact ENNReal.toReal_ofReal (p_pos i)
    · intro b _ bi
      simp [bi]

  d[X₁ ; μ₁ # X₂ ; μ₂] + p.η * d[p.X₀₁ ; ℙ # X₁ ; μ₁] + p.η * d[p.X₀₂ ; ℙ # X₂ ; μ₂]

declarations.doc:
If $X_1,X_2$ are two $G$-valued random variables, then
$$ \tau[X_1; X_2] := d[X_1; X_2] + \eta d[X^0_1; X_1] + \eta d[X^0_2; X_2].$$
Here, $X^0_1$ and $X^0_2$ are two random variables fixed once and for all in most of the argument.
To lighten notation, We package `X^0_1` and `X^0_2` in a single object named `p`.

We denote it as `τ[X₁ ; μ₁ # X₂ ; μ₂ | p]` where `p` is a fixed package containing the information
of the reference random variables. When the measurable spaces have a canonical measure `ℙ`, we
can use `τ[X₁ # X₂ | p]`

result.statement: For $\eta = 1/8$, there exist tau-minimizers $X_1, X_2$ satisfying $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
result.proof: For each $\eta <1/8$, consider minimizers $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ from \Cref{tau-min}. By \Cref{de-prop-improv}, they satisfy $d[X_1^\eta ; X_2^\eta ]=0$. By compactness of the space of probability measures on $G$, one may extract a converging subsequence of the distributions of $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ as $\eta \to 1/8$. By continuity of all the involved quantities, the limit is a pair of tau-minimizers for $1/8$ satisfying additionally $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.

  /-- The constant that parameterizes how good the package is. The argument only works for
  small enough `η`, typically `≤ 1/9` or `< 1/8`. -/
  η : ℝ
  hη : 0 < η
  hη' : 8 * η ≤ 1

variable (p : refPackage Ω₀₁ Ω₀₂ G)
variable {Ω₀₁ Ω₀₂ G}

$$ \tau[X_1; X_2] := d[X_1; X_2] + \eta d[X^0_1; X_1] + \eta d[X^0_2; X_2].$$
Here, $X^0_1$ and $X^0_2$ are two random variables fixed once and for all in most of the argument.
To lighten notation, We package `X^0_1` and `X^0_2` in a single object named `p`.

We denote it as `τ[X₁ ; μ₁ # X₂ ; μ₂ | p]` where `p` is a fixed package containing the information
of the reference random variables. When the measurable spaces have a canonical measure `ℙ`, we
can use `τ[X₁ # X₂ | p]`
-/

defining the τ functional, we will only only need to refer to the package once in the notation
instead of stating the reference spaces, the reference measures and the reference random
variables.

The η parameter has now been incorporated into the package, in preparation for being able to
manipulate the package.

  τ : ℝ

declarations.doc:
A Besicovitch tau-package is a family of balls in a metric space with positive bounded radii,
together with enough data to proceed with the Besicovitch greedy algorithm. We register this in
a single structure to make sure that all our constructions in this algorithm only depend on
one variable.

lemma tendsto_map_of_tendsto_of_continuous {ι : Type*} {L : Filter ι}
    (νs : ι → ProbabilityMeasure Ω) (ν : ProbabilityMeasure Ω) (lim : Tendsto νs L (𝓝 ν))
    {f : Ω → Ω'} (f_cont : Continuous f) :
    Tendsto (fun i ↦ (νs i).map f_cont.measurable.aemeasurable) L
      (𝓝 (ν.map f_cont.measurable.aemeasurable))
declarations.doc:
If `f : X → Y` is continuous and `Y` is equipped with the Borel sigma algebra, then
convergence (in distribution) of `ProbabilityMeasure`s on `X` implies convergence (in
distribution) of the push-forwards of these measures by `f`.

declarations.source_snippet:
theorem tendsto_iff_forall_lintegral_tendsto {γ : Type*} {F : Filter γ}
    {μs : γ → ProbabilityMeasure Ω} {μ : ProbabilityMeasure Ω} :
    Tendsto μs F (𝓝 μ) ↔
      ∀ f : Ω →ᵇ ℝ≥0,
        Tendsto (fun i ↦ ∫⁻ ω, f ω ∂(μs i : Measure Ω)) F (𝓝 (∫⁻ ω, f ω ∂(μ : Measure Ω)))
declarations.doc:
A characterization of weak convergence of probability measures by the condition that the
integrals of every continuous bounded nonnegative function converge to the integral of the function
against the limit measure.

structure refPackage where
  /-- The first variable in a package. -/

  hmeas1 : Measurable X₀₁
  hmeas2 : Measurable X₀₂

  small enough `η`, typically `≤ 1/9` or `< 1/8`. -/
  η : ℝ
  hη : 0 < η
  hη' : 8 * η ≤ 1

variable (p : refPackage Ω₀₁ Ω₀₂ G)
variable {Ω₀₁ Ω₀₂ G}

variable {Ω Ω' Ω₁ Ω₂ Ω'₁ Ω'₂ S T : Type*}

/-- If $X_1,X_2$ are two $G$-valued random variables, then
$$ \tau[X_1; X_2] := d[X_1; X_2] + \eta d[X^0_1; X_1] + \eta d[X^0_2; X_2].$$
Here, $X^0_1$ and $X^0_2$ are two random variables fixed once and for all in most of the argument.
To lighten notation, We package `X^0_1` and `X^0_2` in a single object named `p`.

We denote it as `τ[X₁ ; μ₁ # X₂ ; μ₂ | p]` where `p` is a fixed package containing the information
of the reference random variables. When the measurable spaces have a canonical measure `ℙ`, we
can use `τ[X₁ # X₂ | p]`
-/
declarations.doc:
A structure that packages all the fixed information in the main argument. In this way, when
defining the τ functional, we will only only need to refer to the package once in the notation
instead of stating the reference spaces, the reference measures and the reference random
variables.

The η parameter has now been incorporated into the package, in preparation for being able to
manipulate the package.

A Besicovitch tau-package is a family of balls in a metric space with positive bounded radii,
together with enough data to proceed with the Besicovitch greedy algorithm. We register this in
a single structure to make sure that all our constructions in this algorithm only depend on
one variable.

declarations.doc:
If `f : X → Y` is continuous and `Y` is equipped with the Borel sigma algebra, then
convergence (in distribution) of `ProbabilityMeasure`s on `X` implies convergence (in
distribution) of the push-forwards of these measures by `f`.

declarations.source_snippet:
theorem tendsto_iff_forall_lintegral_tendsto {γ : Type*} {F : Filter γ}
    {μs : γ → ProbabilityMeasure Ω} {μ : ProbabilityMeasure Ω} :
    Tendsto μs F (𝓝 μ) ↔
      ∀ f : Ω →ᵇ ℝ≥0,
        Tendsto (fun i ↦ ∫⁻ ω, f ω ∂(μs i : Measure Ω)) F (𝓝 (∫⁻ ω, f ω ∂(μ : Measure Ω)))
declarations.doc:
A characterization of weak convergence of probability measures by the condition that the
integrals of every continuous bounded nonnegative function converge to the integral of the function
against the limit measure.

result.statement: For $\eta = 1/8$, there exist tau-minimizers $X_1, X_2$ satisfying $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
result.proof: For each $\eta <1/8$, consider minimizers $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ from \Cref{tau-min}. By \Cref{de-prop-improv}, they satisfy $d[X_1^\eta ; X_2^\eta ]=0$. By compactness of the space of probability measures on $G$, one may extract a converging subsequence of the distributions of $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ as $\eta \to 1/8$. By continuity of all the involved quantities, the limit is a pair of tau-minimizers for $1/8$ satisfying additionally $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.

nodes.claim: For a sequence of pairs of probability measures on a finite discrete G, there is a converging subsequence in the weak topology of ProbabilityMeasure G × ProbabilityMeasure G.
nodes.proof_hint: Use compactness of ProbabilityMeasure G for finite/discrete spaces, or a finite-dimensional closed simplex argument.

nodes.claim: If q n are refPackages with 8*(q n).η<1 and q n → p, and for each n X1n X2n are tau-minimizers for q n with rdist 0, then a subsequence of their probability laws has limits μ,ν; μ,ν are probability laws of measurable functions realizing p.
nodes.proof_hint: Apply P2 to the sequence of law pairs; use continuity of tau and rdist to show the limit laws satisfy tau_minimizes p and rdist 0.

    (X₁ : Ω₁ → G) (X₂ : Ω₂ → G) (μ₁ : Measure Ω₁) (μ₂ : Measure Ω₂) : ℝ :=
  d[X₁ ; μ₁ # X₂ ; μ₂] + p.η * d[p.X₀₁ ; ℙ # X₁ ; μ₁] + p.η * d[p.X₀₂ ; ℙ # X₂ ; μ₂]

declarations.doc:
If $X_1,X_2$ are two $G$-valued random variables, then
$$ \tau[X_1; X_2] := d[X_1; X_2] + \eta d[X^0_1; X_1] + \eta d[X^0_2; X_2].$$
Here, $X^0_1$ and $X^0_2$ are two random variables fixed once and for all in most of the argument.
To lighten notation, We package `X^0_1` and `X^0_2` in a single object named `p`.

We denote it as `τ[X₁ ; μ₁ # X₂ ; μ₂ | p]` where `p` is a fixed package containing the information
of the reference random variables. When the measurable spaces have a canonical measure `ℙ`, we
can use `τ[X₁ # X₂ | p]`

declarations.source_snippet:
structure refPackage where
  /-- The first variable in a package. -/
  X₀₁ : Ω₀₁ → G
  /-- The second variable in a package. -/
  X₀₂ : Ω₀₂ → G
  hmeas1 : Measurable X₀₁
  hmeas2 : Measurable X₀₂
  /-- The constant that parameterizes how good the package is. The argument only works for
  small enough `η`, typically `≤ 1/9` or `< 1/8`. -/
  η : ℝ
  hη : 0 < η
  hη' : 8 * η ≤ 1

variable (p : refPackage Ω₀₁ Ω₀₂ G)
variable {Ω₀₁ Ω₀₂ G}

variable {Ω Ω' Ω₁ Ω₂ Ω'₁ Ω'₂ S T : Type*}

/-- If $X_1,X_2$ are two $G$-valued random variables, then
$$ \tau[X_1; X_2] := d[X_1; X_2] + \eta d[X^0_1; X_1] + \eta d[X^0_2; X_2].$$
Here, $X^0_1$ and $X^0_2$ are two random variables fixed once and for all in most of the argument.
To lighten notation, We package `X^0_1` and `X^0_2` in a single object named `p`.

We denote it as `τ[X₁ ; μ₁ # X₂ ; μ₂ | p]` where `p` is a fixed package containing the information
of the reference random variables. When the measurable spaces have a canonical measure `ℙ`, we
can use `τ[X₁ # X₂ | p]`
-/
declarations.doc:
A structure that packages all the fixed information in the main argument. In this way, when
defining the τ functional, we will only only need to refer to the package once in the notation
instead of stating the reference spaces, the reference measures and the reference random
variables.

The η parameter has now been incorporated into the package, in preparation for being able to
manipulate the package.

declarations.name: Besicovitch.TauPackage
declarations.source_snippet:
structure TauPackage (β : Type*) (α : Type*) extends BallPackage β α where
  τ : ℝ
  one_lt_tau : 1 < τ
declarations.doc:
A Besicovitch tau-package is a family of balls in a metric space with positive bounded radii,
together with enough data to proceed with the Besicovitch greedy algorithm. We register this in
a single structure to make sure that all our constructions in this algorithm only depend on
one variable.

declarations.name: Besicovitch.TauPackage.lastStep_nonempty
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem lastStep_nonempty :
    {i | ¬∃ b : β, p.c b ∉ p.iUnionUpTo i ∧ p.R i ≤ p.τ * p.r b}.Nonempty

declarations.name: Besicovitch.TauPackage.monotone_iUnionUpTo
declarations.source_snippet: theorem monotone_iUnionUpTo : Monotone p.iUnionUpTo

declarations.name: Besicovitch.TauPackage.R
declarations.source_snippet:
def R (i : Ordinal.{u}) : ℝ :=
  iSup fun b : { b : β // p.c b ∉ p.iUnionUpTo i } => p.r b
declarations.doc: Supremum of the radii of balls whose centers are not yet covered at step `i`.

declarations.name: Besicovitch.TauPackage.iUnionUpTo
declarations.source_snippet:
def iUnionUpTo (i : Ordinal.{u}) : Set α :=
  ⋃ j : { j // j < i }, ball (p.c (p.index j)) (p.r (p.index j))
declarations.doc: The set of points that are covered by the union of balls selected at steps `< i`.

result.statement: For $\eta = 1/8$, there exist tau-minimizers $X_1, X_2$ satisfying $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
result.proof: For each $\eta <1/8$, consider minimizers $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ from \Cref{tau-min}. By \Cref{de-prop-improv}, they satisfy $d[X_1^\eta ; X_2^\eta ]=0$. By compactness of the space of probability measures on $G$, one may extract a converging subsequence of the distributions of $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ as $\eta \to 1/8$. By continuity of all the involved quantities, the limit is a pair of tau-minimizers for $1/8$ satisfying additionally $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.

nodes.proof_hint: Take Ω = G × G with the product measure μ.prod ν, X₁ = fst and X₂ = snd, and use projection measurability and probability product instance.

nodes.claim: If q n are refPackages with 8*(q n).η<1 and q n → p, and for each n X1n X2n are tau-minimizers for q n with rdist 0, then a subsequence of their probability laws has limits μ,ν; μ,ν are probability laws of measurable functions realizing p.

result.statement: For $\eta = 1/8$, there exist tau-minimizers $X_1, X_2$ satisfying $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
result.proof: For each $\eta <1/8$, consider minimizers $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ from \Cref{tau-min}. By \Cref{de-prop-improv}, they satisfy $d[X_1^\eta ; X_2^\eta ]=0$. By compactness of the space of probability measures on $G$, one may extract a converging subsequence of the distributions of $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ as $\eta \to 1/8$. By continuity of all the involved quantities, the limit is a pair of tau-minimizers for $1/8$ satisfying additionally $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.

nodes.claim: For any probability measures μ ν on finite G, there is a probability space Ω and measurable X₁ X₂ on Ω whose laws are μ and ν respectively.
nodes.proof_hint: Take Ω = G × G with the product measure μ.prod ν, X₁ = fst and X₂ = snd, and use projection measurability and probability product instance.

nodes.proof_hint: Use tau_minimizer_exists q and tau_strictly_decreases'.

nodes.claim: For a sequence of pairs of probability measures on a finite discrete G, there is a converging subsequence in the weak topology of ProbabilityMeasure G × ProbabilityMeasure G.
nodes.proof_hint: Use compactness of ProbabilityMeasure G for finite/discrete spaces, or a finite-dimensional closed simplex argument.

nodes.claim: If q n are refPackages with 8*(q n).η<1 and q n → p, and for each n X1n X2n are tau-minimizers for q n with rdist 0, then a subsequence of their probability laws has limits μ,ν; μ,ν are probability laws of measurable functions realizing p.

result.statement: For $\eta = 1/8$, there exist tau-minimizers $X_1, X_2$ satisfying $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
result.proof: For each $\eta <1/8$, consider minimizers $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ from \Cref{tau-min}. By \Cref{de-prop-improv}, they satisfy $d[X_1^\eta ; X_2^\eta ]=0$. By compactness of the space of probability measures on $G$, one may extract a converging subsequence of the distributions of $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ as $\eta \to 1/8$. By continuity of all the involved quantities, the limit is a pair of tau-minimizers for $1/8$ satisfying additionally $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.

nodes.proof_hint: Set q n.η = p.η*(something below 1) or p.η - 1/n+, preserving X₀₁, X₀₂ and using refPackage constructor.

nodes.claim: For any probability measures μ ν on finite G, there is a probability space Ω and measurable X₁ X₂ on Ω whose laws are μ and ν respectively.
nodes.proof_hint: Take Ω = G × G with the product measure μ.prod ν, X₁ = fst and X₂ = snd, and use projection measurability and probability product instance.

nodes.claim: For any refPackage q with 8 * q.η < 1, there exist measurable probability-space variables X₁, X₂ with tau_minimizes q X₁ X₂ and d[X₁ # X₂] = 0.
nodes.proof_hint: Use tau_minimizer_exists q and tau_strictly_decreases'.

nodes.claim: For a sequence of pairs of probability measures on a finite discrete G, there is a converging subsequence in the weak topology of ProbabilityMeasure G × ProbabilityMeasure G.
nodes.proof_hint: Use compactness of ProbabilityMeasure G for finite/discrete spaces, or a finite-dimensional closed simplex argument.

nodes.claim: If q n are refPackages with 8*(q n).η<1 and q n → p, and for each n X1n X2n are tau-minimizers for q n with rdist 0, then a subsequence of their probability laws has limits μ,ν; μ,ν are probability laws of measurable functions realizing p.
nodes.proof_hint: Apply P2 to the sequence of law pairs; use continuity of tau and rdist to show the limit laws satisfy tau_minimizes p and rdist 0.

result.statement: For $\eta = 1/8$, there exist tau-minimizers $X_1, X_2$ satisfying $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
result.proof: For each $\eta <1/8$, consider minimizers $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ from \Cref{tau-min}. By \Cref{de-prop-improv}, they satisfy $d[X_1^\eta ; X_2^\eta ]=0$. By compactness of the space of probability measures on $G$, one may extract a converging subsequence of the distributions of $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ as $\eta \to 1/8$. By continuity of all the involved quantities, the limit is a pair of tau-minimizers for $1/8$ satisfying additionally $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.

result.statement: For $\eta = 1/8$, there exist tau-minimizers $X_1, X_2$ satisfying $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
result.proof: For each $\eta <1/8$, consider minimizers $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ from \Cref{tau-min}. By \Cref{de-prop-improv}, they satisfy $d[X_1^\eta ; X_2^\eta ]=0$. By compactness of the space of probability measures on $G$, one may extract a converging subsequence of the distributions of $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ as $\eta \to 1/8$. By continuity of all the involved quantities, the limit is a pair of tau-minimizers for $1/8$ satisfying additionally $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.

nodes.claim: For any probability measures μ ν on finite G, there is a probability space Ω and measurable X₁ X₂ on Ω whose laws are μ and ν respectively.

nodes.proof_hint: Use tau_minimizer_exists q and tau_strictly_decreases'.

nodes.claim: For a sequence of pairs of probability measures on a finite discrete G, there is a converging subsequence in the weak topology of ProbabilityMeasure G × ProbabilityMeasure G.
nodes.proof_hint: Use compactness of ProbabilityMeasure G for finite/discrete spaces, or a finite-dimensional closed simplex argument.

nodes.claim: If q n are refPackages with 8*(q n).η<1 and q n → p, and for each n X1n X2n are tau-minimizers for q n with rdist 0, then a subsequence of their probability laws has limits μ,ν; μ,ν are probability laws of measurable functions realizing p.

result.statement: For $\eta = 1/8$, there exist tau-minimizers $X_1, X_2$ satisfying $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
result.proof: For each $\eta <1/8$, consider minimizers $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ from \Cref{tau-min}. By \Cref{de-prop-improv}, they satisfy $d[X_1^\eta ; X_2^\eta ]=0$. By compactness of the space of probability measures on $G$, one may extract a converging subsequence of the distributions of $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ as $\eta \to 1/8$. By continuity of all the involved quantities, the limit is a pair of tau-minimizers for $1/8$ satisfying additionally $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.

result.statement: For $\eta = 1/8$, there exist tau-minimizers $X_1, X_2$ satisfying $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
result.proof: For each $\eta <1/8$, consider minimizers $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ from \Cref{tau-min}. By \Cref{de-prop-improv}, they satisfy $d[X_1^\eta ; X_2^\eta ]=0$. By compactness of the space of probability measures on $G$, one may extract a converging subsequence of the distributions of $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ as $\eta \to 1/8$. By continuity of all the involved quantities, the limit is a pair of tau-minimizers for $1/8$ satisfying additionally $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.

nodes.claim: There is a sequence q : ℕ → refPackage Ω₀₁ Ω₀₂ G with 8*(q n).η < 1 for all n and (q n).η → p.η, using p for the base random variables.
nodes.proof_hint: Set q n.η = p.η*(something below 1) or p.η - 1/n+, preserving X₀₁, X₀₂ and using refPackage constructor.

nodes.claim: For any probability measures μ ν on finite G, there is a probability space Ω and measurable X₁ X₂ on Ω whose laws are μ and ν respectively.
nodes.proof_hint: Take Ω = G × G with the product measure μ.prod ν, X₁ = fst and X₂ = snd, and use projection measurability and probability product instance.

nodes.claim: For any refPackage q with 8 * q.η < 1, there exist measurable probability-space variables X₁, X₂ with tau_minimizes q X₁ X₂ and d[X₁ # X₂] = 0.
nodes.proof_hint: Use tau_minimizer_exists q and tau_strictly_decreases'.

nodes.claim: For a sequence of pairs of probability measures on a finite discrete G, there is a converging subsequence in the weak topology of ProbabilityMeasure G × ProbabilityMeasure G.
nodes.proof_hint: Use compactness of ProbabilityMeasure G for finite/discrete spaces, or a finite-dimensional closed simplex argument.

nodes.claim: If q n are refPackages with 8*(q n).η<1 and q n → p, and for each n X1n X2n are tau-minimizers for q n with rdist 0, then a subsequence of their probability laws has limits μ,ν; μ,ν are probability laws of measurable functions realizing p.
nodes.proof_hint: Apply P2 to the sequence of law pairs; use continuity of tau and rdist to show the limit laws satisfy tau_minimizes p and rdist 0.

result.statement: For $\eta = 1/8$, there exist tau-minimizers $X_1, X_2$ satisfying $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
result.proof: For each $\eta <1/8$, consider minimizers $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ from \Cref{tau-min}. By \Cref{de-prop-improv}, they satisfy $d[X_1^\eta ; X_2^\eta ]=0$. By compactness of the space of probability measures on $G$, one may extract a converging subsequence of the distributions of $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ as $\eta \to 1/8$. By continuity of all the involved quantities, the limit is a pair of tau-minimizers for $1/8$ satisfying additionally $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.

result.statement: For $\eta = 1/8$, there exist tau-minimizers $X_1, X_2$ satisfying $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
result.proof: For each $\eta <1/8$, consider minimizers $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ from \Cref{tau-min}. By \Cref{de-prop-improv}, they satisfy $d[X_1^\eta ; X_2^\eta ]=0$. By compactness of the space of probability measures on $G$, one may extract a converging subsequence of the distributions of $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ as $\eta \to 1/8$. By continuity of all the involved quantities, the limit is a pair of tau-minimizers for $1/8$ satisfying additionally $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.

result.statement: For $\eta = 1/8$, there exist tau-minimizers $X_1, X_2$ satisfying $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
result.proof: For each $\eta <1/8$, consider minimizers $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ from \Cref{tau-min}. By \Cref{de-prop-improv}, they satisfy $d[X_1^\eta ; X_2^\eta ]=0$. By compactness of the space of probability measures on $G$, one may extract a converging subsequence of the distributions of $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ as $\eta \to 1/8$. By continuity of all the involved quantities, the limit is a pair of tau-minimizers for $1/8$ satisfying additionally $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.

nodes.claim: For any probability measures μ ν on finite G, there is a probability space Ω and measurable X₁ X₂ on Ω whose laws are μ and ν respectively.
nodes.proof_hint: Take Ω = G × G with the product measure μ.prod ν, X₁ = fst and X₂ = snd, and use projection measurability and probability product instance.

result.statement: For $\eta = 1/8$, there exist tau-minimizers $X_1, X_2$ satisfying $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
result.proof: For each $\eta <1/8$, consider minimizers $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ from \Cref{tau-min}. By \Cref{de-prop-improv}, they satisfy $d[X_1^\eta ; X_2^\eta ]=0$. By compactness of the space of probability measures on $G$, one may extract a converging subsequence of the distributions of $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ as $\eta \to 1/8$. By continuity of all the involved quantities, the limit is a pair of tau-minimizers for $1/8$ satisfying additionally $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.

nodes.claim: For any probability measures μ ν on finite G, there is a probability space Ω and measurable X₁ X₂ on Ω whose laws are μ and ν respectively.
nodes.proof_hint: Take Ω = G × G with the product measure μ.prod ν, X₁ = fst and X₂ = snd, and use projection measurability and probability product instance.

nodes.claim: For any refPackage q with 8 * q.η < 1, there exist measurable probability-space variables X₁, X₂ with tau_minimizes q X₁ X₂ and d[X₁ # X₂] = 0.
nodes.proof_hint: Use tau_minimizer_exists q and tau_strictly_decreases'.

nodes.claim: For a sequence of pairs of probability measures on a finite discrete G, there is a converging subsequence in the weak topology of ProbabilityMeasure G × ProbabilityMeasure G.
nodes.proof_hint: Use compactness of ProbabilityMeasure G for finite/discrete spaces, or a finite-dimensional closed simplex argument.

nodes.claim: If q n are refPackages with 8*(q n).η<1 and q n → p, and for each n X1n X2n are tau-minimizers for q n with rdist 0, then a subsequence of their probability laws has limits μ,ν; μ,ν are probability laws of measurable functions realizing p.
nodes.proof_hint: Apply P2 to the sequence of law pairs; use continuity of tau and rdist to show the limit laws satisfy tau_minimizes p and rdist 0.

lemma ProofSteps.P4.{u_1, u_2, uG}
    {Ω₀₁ : Type u_1} {Ω₀₂ : Type u_2}
    [mΩ₀₁ : MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace Ω₀₁]
    [mΩ₀₂ : MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace Ω₀₂]
    {G : Type uG} [MeasurableSpace G]
    (p : refPackage Ω₀₁ Ω₀₂ G) :
    ∃ q : ℕ → refPackage Ω₀₁ Ω₀₂ G,
      (∀ n, 8 * (q n).η < 1) ∧
        Filter.Tendsto (fun n => (q n).η) Filter.atTop (nhds p.η)

lemma ProofSteps.P6 {G : Type uG} [MeasurableSpace G]
    (μ ν : MeasureTheory.Measure G)
    [hμ : MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    [hν : MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure ν] :
    ∃ (Ω : Type uG) (mΩ : MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace Ω) (X₁ X₂ : Ω → G),
      Measurable X₁ ∧ Measurable X₂ ∧
      MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure (@MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume Ω mΩ) ∧
      MeasureTheory.Measure.map X₁ (@MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume Ω mΩ) = μ ∧
      MeasureTheory.Measure.map X₂ (@MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume Ω mΩ) = ν

lemma ProofSteps.P1.{u_1, u_2, uG}
    {Ω₀₁ : Type u_1} {Ω₀₂ : Type u_2} [mΩ₀₁ : MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace Ω₀₁] [mΩ₀₂ : MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace Ω₀₂]
    [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure (@MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume Ω₀₁ mΩ₀₁)]
    [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure (@MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume Ω₀₂ mΩ₀₂)]
    {G : Type uG} [AddCommGroup G] [Module (ZMod 2) G] [Fintype G] [MeasurableSpace G]
    [MeasurableSingletonClass G] (q : refPackage Ω₀₁ Ω₀₂ G) (hq : 8 * q.η < 1) :
    ∃ (Ω : Type uG) (mΩ : MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace Ω) (X₁ : Ω → G) (X₂ : Ω → G),
      Measurable X₁ ∧ Measurable X₂ ∧
        MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure (@MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume Ω mΩ) ∧
        tau_minimizes q X₁ X₂ ∧ d[X₁ # X₂] = 0

lemma ProofSteps.P2.{uG}
    {G : Type uG} [Fintype G] [MeasurableSpace G] [MeasurableSingletonClass G]
    [TopologicalSpace G] [DiscreteTopology G] [BorelSpace G] [OpensMeasurableSpace G]
    (x : ℕ → MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure G × MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure G) :
    ∃ (μ ν : MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure G) (φ : ℕ → ℕ),
      StrictMono φ ∧
        Filter.Tendsto (fun n => (x (φ n)).1) Filter.atTop (nhds μ) ∧
        Filter.Tendsto (fun n => (x (φ n)).2) Filter.atTop (nhds ν)

Missing assumption that for each n there are tau-minimizers X1n X2n for q n with rdist 0; missing subsequence/law-limit conclusion relating μ,ν to those minimizers.
The natural-language theorem assumes, for each n, the existence of random variables X1n, X2n that are tau-minimizers for q n and have rdist 0, and then concludes that a subsequence of their probability laws has limits μ,ν which are probability laws of measurable functions realizing p. The candidate statement omits the hypotheses about X1n and X2n entirely and does not mention subsequences or limits of their laws. It only assumes the q n package conditions and η convergence, then directly concludes existence of some measurable X₁,X₂ that minimize τ for p and have d=0. This is a different theorem: the conclusion is not tied to the laws of the given minimizers for q n.

result.statement: For $\eta = 1/8$, there exist tau-minimizers $X_1, X_2$ satisfying $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
result.proof: For each $\eta <1/8$, consider minimizers $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ from \Cref{tau-min}. By \Cref{de-prop-improv}, they satisfy $d[X_1^\eta ; X_2^\eta ]=0$. By compactness of the space of probability measures on $G$, one may extract a converging subsequence of the distributions of $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ as $\eta \to 1/8$. By continuity of all the involved quantities, the limit is a pair of tau-minimizers for $1/8$ satisfying additionally $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.

nodes.proof_hint: Take Ω = G × G with the product measure μ.prod ν, X₁ = fst and X₂ = snd, and use projection measurability and probability product instance.

nodes.proof_hint: Use compactness of ProbabilityMeasure G for finite/discrete spaces, or a finite-dimensional closed simplex argument.

lemma ProofSteps.P6 {G : Type uG} [MeasurableSpace G]
    (μ ν : MeasureTheory.Measure G)
    [hμ : MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    [hν : MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure ν] :
    ∃ (Ω : Type uG) (mΩ : MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace Ω) (X₁ X₂ : Ω → G),
      Measurable X₁ ∧ Measurable X₂ ∧
      MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure (@MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume Ω mΩ) ∧
      MeasureTheory.Measure.map X₁ (@MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume Ω mΩ) = μ ∧
      MeasureTheory.Measure.map X₂ (@MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume Ω mΩ) = ν

    {Ω₀₁ : Type u_1} {Ω₀₂ : Type u_2} [mΩ₀₁ : MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace Ω₀₁] [mΩ₀₂ : MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace Ω₀₂]

    [MeasurableSingletonClass G] (q : refPackage Ω₀₁ Ω₀₂ G) (hq : 8 * q.η < 1) :
    ∃ (Ω : Type uG) (mΩ : MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace Ω) (X₁ : Ω → G) (X₂ : Ω → G),
      Measurable X₁ ∧ Measurable X₂ ∧
        MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure (@MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume Ω mΩ) ∧
        tau_minimizes q X₁ X₂ ∧ d[X₁ # X₂] = 0

lemma ProofSteps.P2.{uG}

    [TopologicalSpace G] [DiscreteTopology G] [BorelSpace G] [OpensMeasurableSpace G]
    (x : ℕ → MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure G × MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure G) :

nodes.claim: There is a sequence q : ℕ → refPackage Ω₀₁ Ω₀₂ G with 8*(q n).η < 1 for all n and (q n).η → p.η, using p for the base random variables.
nodes.proof_hint: Set q n.η = p.η*(something below 1) or p.η - 1/n+, preserving X₀₁, X₀₂ and using refPackage constructor.

nodes.claim: For any probability measures μ ν on finite G, there is a probability space Ω and measurable X₁ X₂ on Ω whose laws are μ and ν respectively.
nodes.proof_hint: Take Ω = G × G with the product measure μ.prod ν, X₁ = fst and X₂ = snd, and use projection measurability and probability product instance.

nodes.claim: For any refPackage q with 8 * q.η < 1, there exist measurable probability-space variables X₁, X₂ with tau_minimizes q X₁ X₂ and d[X₁ # X₂] = 0.
nodes.proof_hint: Use tau_minimizer_exists q and tau_strictly_decreases'.

nodes.claim: For a sequence of pairs of probability measures on a finite discrete G, there is a converging subsequence in the weak topology of ProbabilityMeasure G × ProbabilityMeasure G.
nodes.proof_hint: Use compactness of ProbabilityMeasure G for finite/discrete spaces, or a finite-dimensional closed simplex argument.

nodes.claim: If q n are refPackages with 8*(q n).η<1 and q n → p, and for each n X1n X2n are tau-minimizers for q n with rdist 0, then a subsequence of their probability laws has limits μ,ν; μ,ν are probability laws of measurable functions realizing p.
nodes.proof_hint: Apply P2 to the sequence of law pairs; use continuity of tau and rdist to show the limit laws satisfy tau_minimizes p and rdist 0.

By continuity of all the involved quantities, the limit is a pair of tau-minimizers for $1/8$ satisfying additionally $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.

result.statement: For $\eta = 1/8$, there exist tau-minimizers $X_1, X_2$ satisfying $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
result.proof: For each $\eta <1/8$, consider minimizers $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ from \Cref{tau-min}. By \Cref{de-prop-improv}, they satisfy $d[X_1^\eta ; X_2^\eta ]=0$. By compactness of the space of probability measures on $G$, one may extract a converging subsequence of the distributions of $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ as $\eta \to 1/8$. By continuity of all the involved quantities, the limit is a pair of tau-minimizers for $1/8$ satisfying additionally $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.

result.proof: For each $\eta <1/8$, consider minimizers $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ from \Cref{tau-min}. By \Cref{de-prop-improv}, they satisfy $d[X_1^\eta ; X_2^\eta ]=0$. nodes.claim: For a sequence of pairs of probability measures on a finite discrete G, there is a converging subsequence in the weak topology of ProbabilityMeasure G × ProbabilityMeasure G.
nodes.proof_hint: Use compactness of ProbabilityMeasure G for finite/discrete spaces, or a finite-dimensional closed simplex argument.

nodes.claim: If q n are refPackages with 8*(q n).η<1 and q n → p, and for each n X1n X2n are tau-minimizers for q n with rdist 0, then a subsequence of their probability laws has limits μ,ν; μ,ν are probability laws of measurable functions realizing p.

result.statement: For $\eta = 1/8$, there exist tau-minimizers $X_1, X_2$ satisfying $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
result.proof: For each $\eta <1/8$, consider minimizers $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ from \Cref{tau-min}. By \Cref{de-prop-improv}, they satisfy $d[X_1^\eta ; X_2^\eta ]=0$. By compactness of the space of probability measures on $G$, one may extract a converging subsequence of the distributions of $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ as $\eta \to 1/8$. By continuity of all the involved quantities, the limit is a pair of tau-minimizers for $1/8$ satisfying additionally $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.

variable (p : refPackage Ω₀₁ Ω₀₂ G)
variable {Ω₀₁ Ω₀₂ G}

/-- If $X_1,X_2$ are two $G$-valued random variables, then
$$ \tau[X_1; X_2] := d[X_1; X_2] + \eta d[X^0_1; X_1] + \eta d[X^0_2; X_2].$$
Here, $X^0_1$ and $X^0_2$ are two random variables fixed once and for all in most of the argument.
To lighten notation, We package `X^0_1` and `X^0_2` in a single object named `p`.

We denote it as `τ[X₁ ; μ₁ # X₂ ; μ₂ | p]` where `p` is a fixed package containing the information
of the reference random variables. When the measurable spaces have a canonical measure `ℙ`, we
can use `τ[X₁ # X₂ | p]`
-/
declarations.doc:
A structure that packages all the fixed information in the main argument. In this way, when
defining the τ functional, we will only only need to refer to the package once in the notation
instead of stating the reference spaces, the reference measures and the reference random
variables.

The η parameter has now been incorporated into the package, in preparation for being able to
manipulate the package.

declarations.name: refPackage
declarations.source_snippet:
structure refPackage where
  /-- The first variable in a package. -/
  X₀₁ : Ω₀₁ → G
  /-- The second variable in a package. -/
  X₀₂ : Ω₀₂ → G
  hmeas1 : Measurable X₀₁
  hmeas2 : Measurable X₀₂
  /-- The constant that parameterizes how good the package is. The argument only works for
  small enough `η`, typically `≤ 1/9` or `< 1/8`. -/
  η : ℝ
  hη : 0 < η
  hη' : 8 * η ≤ 1

variable (p : refPackage Ω₀₁ Ω₀₂ G)
variable {Ω₀₁ Ω₀₂ G}

variable {Ω Ω' Ω₁ Ω₂ Ω'₁ Ω'₂ S T : Type*}

/-- If $X_1,X_2$ are two $G$-valued random variables, then
$$ \tau[X_1; X_2] := d[X_1; X_2] + \eta d[X^0_1; X_1] + \eta d[X^0_2; X_2].$$
Here, $X^0_1$ and $X^0_2$ are two random variables fixed once and for all in most of the argument.
To lighten notation, We package `X^0_1` and `X^0_2` in a single object named `p`.

We denote it as `τ[X₁ ; μ₁ # X₂ ; μ₂ | p]` where `p` is a fixed package containing the information
of the reference random variables. When the measurable spaces have a canonical measure `ℙ`, we
can use `τ[X₁ # X₂ | p]`
-/
declarations.doc:
A structure that packages all the fixed information in the main argument. In this way, when
defining the τ functional, we will only only need to refer to the package once in the notation
instead of stating the reference spaces, the reference measures and the reference random
variables.

The η parameter has now been incorporated into the package, in preparation for being able to
manipulate the package.

  d[X₁ ; μ₁ # X₂ ; μ₂] + p.η * d[p.X₀₁ ; ℙ # X₁ ; μ₁] + p.η * d[p.X₀₂ ; ℙ # X₂ ; μ₂]

declarations.name: Besicovitch.TauPackage
declarations.source_snippet:
structure TauPackage (β : Type*) (α : Type*) extends BallPackage β α where
  τ : ℝ
  one_lt_tau : 1 < τ
declarations.doc:
A Besicovitch tau-package is a family of balls in a metric space with positive bounded radii,
together with enough data to proceed with the Besicovitch greedy algorithm. We register this in
a single structure to make sure that all our constructions in this algorithm only depend on
one variable.

declarations.name: Besicovitch.TauPackage.lastStep_nonempty
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem lastStep_nonempty :
    {i | ¬∃ b : β, p.c b ∉ p.iUnionUpTo i ∧ p.R i ≤ p.τ * p.r b}.Nonempty

declarations.name: Besicovitch.TauPackage.R
declarations.source_snippet:
def R (i : Ordinal.{u}) : ℝ :=
  iSup fun b : { b : β // p.c b ∉ p.iUnionUpTo i } => p.r b
declarations.doc: Supremum of the radii of balls whose centers are not yet covered at step `i`.

declarations.name: Besicovitch.TauPackage.iUnionUpTo
declarations.source_snippet:
def iUnionUpTo (i : Ordinal.{u}) : Set α :=
  ⋃ j : { j // j < i }, ball (p.c (p.index j)) (p.r (p.index j))
declarations.doc: The set of points that are covered by the union of balls selected at steps `< i`.

result.statement: For $\eta = 1/8$, there exist tau-minimizers $X_1, X_2$ satisfying $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
result.proof: For each $\eta <1/8$, consider minimizers $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ from \Cref{tau-min}. By \Cref{de-prop-improv}, they satisfy $d[X_1^\eta ; X_2^\eta ]=0$. By compactness of the space of probability measures on $G$, one may extract a converging subsequence of the distributions of $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ as $\eta \to 1/8$. By continuity of all the involved quantities, the limit is a pair of tau-minimizers for $1/8$ satisfying additionally $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.

result.statement: For $\eta = 1/8$, there exist tau-minimizers $X_1, X_2$ satisfying $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
result.proof: For each $\eta <1/8$, consider minimizers $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ from \Cref{tau-min}. By \Cref{de-prop-improv}, they satisfy $d[X_1^\eta ; X_2^\eta ]=0$. By compactness of the space of probability measures on $G$, one may extract a converging subsequence of the distributions of $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ as $\eta \to 1/8$. By continuity of all the involved quantities, the limit is a pair of tau-minimizers for $1/8$ satisfying additionally $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.

result.statement: For $\eta = 1/8$, there exist tau-minimizers $X_1, X_2$ satisfying $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
result.proof: For each $\eta <1/8$, consider minimizers $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ from \Cref{tau-min}. By \Cref{de-prop-improv}, they satisfy $d[X_1^\eta ; X_2^\eta ]=0$. By compactness of the space of probability measures on $G$, one may extract a converging subsequence of the distributions of $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ as $\eta \to 1/8$. By continuity of all the involved quantities, the limit is a pair of tau-minimizers for $1/8$ satisfying additionally $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.

result.statement: For $\eta = 1/8$, there exist tau-minimizers $X_1, X_2$ satisfying $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
result.proof: For each $\eta <1/8$, consider minimizers $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ from \Cref{tau-min}. By \Cref{de-prop-improv}, they satisfy $d[X_1^\eta ; X_2^\eta ]=0$. By compactness of the space of probability measures on $G$, one may extract a converging subsequence of the distributions of $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ as $\eta \to 1/8$. By continuity of all the involved quantities, the limit is a pair of tau-minimizers for $1/8$ satisfying additionally $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.

lemma tendsto_map_of_tendsto_of_continuous {ι : Type*} {L : Filter ι}
    (νs : ι → ProbabilityMeasure Ω) (ν : ProbabilityMeasure Ω) (lim : Tendsto νs L (𝓝 ν))
    {f : Ω → Ω'} (f_cont : Continuous f) :
    Tendsto (fun i ↦ (νs i).map f_cont.measurable.aemeasurable) L
      (𝓝 (ν.map f_cont.measurable.aemeasurable))
declarations.doc:
If `f : X → Y` is continuous and `Y` is equipped with the Borel sigma algebra, then
convergence (in distribution) of `ProbabilityMeasure`s on `X` implies convergence (in
distribution) of the push-forwards of these measures by `f`.

declarations.source_snippet:
theorem tendsto_iff_forall_lintegral_tendsto {γ : Type*} {F : Filter γ}
    {μs : γ → ProbabilityMeasure Ω} {μ : ProbabilityMeasure Ω} :
    Tendsto μs F (𝓝 μ) ↔
      ∀ f : Ω →ᵇ ℝ≥0,
        Tendsto (fun i ↦ ∫⁻ ω, f ω ∂(μs i : Measure Ω)) F (𝓝 (∫⁻ ω, f ω ∂(μ : Measure Ω)))
declarations.doc:
A characterization of weak convergence of probability measures by the condition that the
integrals of every continuous bounded nonnegative function converge to the integral of the function
against the limit measure.

result.statement: For $\eta = 1/8$, there exist tau-minimizers $X_1, X_2$ satisfying $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
result.proof: For each $\eta <1/8$, consider minimizers $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ from \Cref{tau-min}. By \Cref{de-prop-improv}, they satisfy $d[X_1^\eta ; X_2^\eta ]=0$. By compactness of the space of probability measures on $G$, one may extract a converging subsequence of the distributions of $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ as $\eta \to 1/8$. By continuity of all the involved quantities, the limit is a pair of tau-minimizers for $1/8$ satisfying additionally $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.

result.statement: For $\eta = 1/8$, there exist tau-minimizers $X_1, X_2$ satisfying $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
result.proof: For each $\eta <1/8$, consider minimizers $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ from \Cref{tau-min}. By \Cref{de-prop-improv}, they satisfy $d[X_1^\eta ; X_2^\eta ]=0$. By compactness of the space of probability measures on $G$, one may extract a converging subsequence of the distributions of $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ as $\eta \to 1/8$. By continuity of all the involved quantities, the limit is a pair of tau-minimizers for $1/8$ satisfying additionally $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.

result.statement: For $\eta = 1/8$, there exist tau-minimizers $X_1, X_2$ satisfying $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
result.proof: For each $\eta <1/8$, consider minimizers $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ from \Cref{tau-min}. By \Cref{de-prop-improv}, they satisfy $d[X_1^\eta ; X_2^\eta ]=0$. By compactness of the space of probability measures on $G$, one may extract a converging subsequence of the distributions of $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ as $\eta \to 1/8$. By continuity of all the involved quantities, the limit is a pair of tau-minimizers for $1/8$ satisfying additionally $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.

result.statement: For $\eta = 1/8$, there exist tau-minimizers $X_1, X_2$ satisfying $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
result.proof: For each $\eta <1/8$, consider minimizers $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ from \Cref{tau-min}. By \Cref{de-prop-improv}, they satisfy $d[X_1^\eta ; X_2^\eta ]=0$. By compactness of the space of probability measures on $G$, one may extract a converging subsequence of the distributions of $X_1^\eta $ and $X_2^\eta $ as $\eta \to 1/8$. By continuity of all the involved quantities, the limit is a pair of tau-minimizers for $1/8$ satisfying additionally $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
